entry.title: Hierarchical low-rank reparameterization to compress trainable parameters in parameter-efficient fine-tuning.
entry.summary: Hierarchical Low-Rank Reparameterization for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper addresses redundancy in the trainable parameters of parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods. It proposes a hierarchical low-rank reparameterization that reorganizes these parameters into an approximately square matrix and applies low-rank decomposition recursively to form a multi-level, progressively compressed structure. The method is combined with LoRA, DoRA, MoSA, and RaSA and evaluated on commonsense reasoning with LLaMA-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B, and on GSM8K math reasoning with LLaMA-3.1-8B. The authors report better performance than baselines under comparable parameter budgets, and competitive or higher average accuracy across eight commonsense benchmarks when parameter counts are compressed by about an order of magnitude.

entry.title: Test-Time Communication in Trading Agent Swarms: A Study of Convergence and Herding
entry.summary: Test-Time Communication in Trading Agent Swarms arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper studies how 200 independent trading agents from four model families behave under five communication regimes over seven US trading days in October 2026. In two of the four families, communicating groups held far more of the same stocks than isolated groups, and group returns largely reflected those shared holdings. The authors conclude that herding assessments must measure excess convergence against a no-peer baseline, since isolated groups also converged on the same stocks.

entry.title: Tracking how language models learn knowledge during pretraining using point-in-time models
entry.summary: What Improves During Pretraining? Tracking Knowledge Acquisition with Point-in-Time Models arXiv · Oct 28, 2026Language models pretrained on multi-year web data learn general and domain-specific knowledge, but how this happens over training is unclear. The authors use point-in-time models trained on different years' web snapshots to define a temporal variability score (TVS), the coefficient of variation of each item's negative log-likelihood across models. Across six benchmarks and six models, high-TVS items improve faster later in pretraining. At the end of training, high-TVS items outperform low-TVS items in 34 of 36 settings, by an average of 7.3 points of chance-normalized accuracy.

entry.title: TeamGym: A training and evaluation environment for AI agent teams working with distributed information
entry.summary: TeamGym: A Gym for Team Decision-Making by AI Agents with Distributed Information arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper presents TeamGym, an environment for evaluating and training language model agents on team decision problems built from legal, finance, medical, and software engineering corpora. It defines "pivotal information" as a minimal set of facts that is necessary and collectively sufficient for a correct decision, and uses it to measure whether agents identify and integrate such facts. Across 8 models and 12 corpora, distributing pivotal information among participants lowered success rate by 22.9 percentage points on average compared with giving it to a single model. Reinforcement learning on team decision loss improved decision quality and produced emergent coordination in participation, speaker selection, and communication.

entry.title: Honeycomb-Surfels: Compact Hexagonal Primitives for Rendering and 3D Reconstruction
entry.summary: Honeycomb-Surfels: Compact Hexagonal Primitives for Efficient Scene Rendering and Reconstruction arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper introduces Hexels, planar hexagonal surface elements with a first-order color field, for efficient representation of 3D scenes and 2D images. Across 34 scenes, Hexels improve PSNR over memory-matched 2DGS by 4.53 to 7.38 dB while requiring less training VRAM. For 3D surface reconstruction, Hexels reduce error by 28.9% on 15 DTU scans and achieve a mean F1 of 34.38% on six Tanks and Temples surface scenes, versus 31.72% for 2DGS.

entry.title: ThinkWorld: Using World Imagination to Teach Robots Action Reasoning from Human Videos
entry.summary: ThinkWorld: World Imagination Reinforces Chain-of-Dynamics Reasoning arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces ThinkWorld, a learning framework for Vision-Language-Action robot models. It represents action reasoning as a Chain-of-Dynamics, a sequence of discrete motion tokens linking the current world state to a future state, and reinforces those chains whose predicted futures better match observed outcomes. This lets videos without action labels supply supervision from observed state transitions, so human and robot experience refine the same reasoning space. Experiments in simulation and on real robots show effective human-to-robot transfer and generalization to unseen tasks and environments.

entry.title: Can Discrete Tokens Represent Images Without Semantic Loss? This paper tests whether quantizing visual signals into discrete tokens loses meaning, and proposes a new quantization method.

The effective bit budget of discrete indices is identified as the key factor. The authors propose Factorized Vector Quantization, which uses symmetric parallel codebooks to quantize complementary views of visual features, continuing to improve at larger bit budgets. entry.title: When to Intervene at Test Time: PORTAL, a Controller for Timing Interventions and Label Queries
entry.summary: When Should We Intervene at Test Time? arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies test-time adaptation, where a deployed model's intervention can help some input batches and hurt others. The authors propose PORTAL, a controller that decides when to deploy an intervention, which inputs to label, and when to stop querying labels. Experiments show that it turns an intervention that lowers overall accuracy into a useful choice on selected batches and prevents severe failures from changes in arrival order. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes PORTAL, a controller that decides when to apply a test-time intervention, which inputs to label, and when to stop querying; each label scores all candidate rules at once, and the abstract rep

entry.title: Attention as lattice gauge theory: relations interact only via Wilson loops
entry.summary: Attention as Lattice Gauge Theory: Relations Interact Only Through Wilson Loops arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper argues that if each entity's coordinate frame can be rotated independently, relations interact only through shared cycles, called Wilson loops. From this it derives the unique symmetry-compatible form of edge attention. The authors implement this as holonomy attention on general relational graphs, which infers unobserved S4 relations without training and flags corrupted triangles.

entry.title: KPPax: A Differentiable Kinetic Preprocessor for Machine Learning in Atmospheric Chemistry
entry.summary: KPPax: preprocess differentiable kinetic ODE for machine learning in atmospheric chemistry arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents KPPax, a tool that converts atmospheric chemical mechanisms written in the Kinetic PreProcessor language into differentiable, just-in-time compiled, vectorisable JAX code. It obtains exact sensitivities through the implicit solvers and forward- and reverse-mode adjoints of the diffrax library, without hand-derived adjoint code. The authors demonstrate it on the POLLU benchmark mechanism, using Fisher information to assess which rate coefficients can be identified and a neural-network correction of an emission inventory trained offline and fine-tuned online.

entry.title: A study on dexterous in-hand object pose reaching that balances skill and safety
entry.summary: Pushing Dexterity and Safety for In-Hand Object Pose Reaching That Works Remarkably Well arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper addresses in-hand object pose reaching, where a multi-fingered LEAP hand moves an object to target positions and orientations. The policies are trained in simulation without human data and transferred zero-shot to the real hand. A learned residual safety filter with adjustable conservativeness reduces object drops by 75% while still reaching 91.5% of goals.

entry.title: GEPA-Curator: A framework for curated learning in self-improving AI agents
entry.summary: GEPA-Curator: Curated Learning for Self Improving Agents arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes GEPA-Curator, a framework that improves how prompts are optimized for large language model agents. It filters out tasks likely to give noisy or unreliable learning signals and retrieves past successful trajectories for a task as extra context for the prompt optimizer. The method was evaluated on GoBrowse, ALFWorld, AppWorld, and τ-bench using Gemini 3.1 Pro and Claude Opus 5 as optimizer models. It matches or exceeds the mean performance of both baselines, with gains of up to 20.7% over GEPA and 21.2% over ACE.

entry.title: Can LLMs Find Hidden Physics Through Free Exploration?
entry.summary: Can LLMs Uncover Hidden Physical Laws through Free Exploration? arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper introduces LongChang, an automated framework that builds simulated worlds where some physical laws are altered. Large language models act as explorers, manipulating objects and building tools to pursue their own questions without task instructions or hints. Among 12 tested models, GPT-6-Astra achieves a 16.7% discovery rate, while the other 11 score 0%. The exploration records show that some anomalies remain uninvestigated and that the altered laws are only partially identified.

entry.title: Scaling laws for tool-use AI agents trained on controllable synthetic environments
entry.summary: Scaling Laws for Tool-Use Agents via Controllable Environment Synthesis arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies how to train large language model agents that complete complex, multi-step tasks using tools. The authors propose SynthAPI, a pipeline that controls the diversity of generated tools, tasks, and databases, and run 458,752 tasks across 849 models of four sizes to derive a scaling law predicting generalization. They find that as data budgets grow, increasing tool and database diversity helps more than adding tasks, and higher data complexity yields larger gains. Agents trained this way outperform models trained on prior work's data across four evaluation benchmarks.

entry.title: MuonGS: Pretraining LLMs with Relaxed Weight-Norm Control
entry.summary: MuonGS: Pretraining LLMs with Relaxed Weight-Norm Control arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper analyzes how weight-norm control affects the Muon optimizer in language model pretraining, using an accumulated effective learning rate as the main tool. It compares vanilla Muon, MuonW, and MuonH, and proposes MuonGS, which uses Gram–Schmidt projection to remove the radial component of each update without fixing the weight norm. In pretraining experiments on dense and MoE models, MuonGS achieves lower validation perplexity than MuonH at long training horizons, with an estimated token-equivalent speedup of up to about 15% for the dense model at matched validation loss.

entry.title: Multi-State Linear Attention with Generalized Second-Order Routing: A Method for Better Long-Sequence Modeling
entry.summary: Multi-State Linear Attention with Generalized Second-Order Routing arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper addresses the quadratic cost of self-attention in long-sequence modeling by improving Multi-State Linear Attention (MSLA). The proposed MERLIN method tracks the first and second moments of each segment's keys, so a query can recover both the mean and variance of its alignment with each segment. Experiments on multi-state variants of Gated DeltaNet-1.3B and Mamba-2-780M show that MERLIN outperforms existing aggregation methods across various long-context tasks.

entry.title: Metacognitive Decoding: A Controller That Makes Diffusion Language Agents More Efficient
entry.summary: Metacognitive Decoding: Efficient Inference for Diffusion Language Agents arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces a metacognitive controller, a lightweight plug-in for diffusion language models, that guides generation based on the needs of the current response and the agent's interaction with its environment. It learns when to finalize tokens and how far generation should extend. Trained on agent trajectories to balance correctness and generation cost, the controller reduces inference FLOPs by 20.6% on average across five benchmarks compared with the most efficient baseline, while keeping task accuracy competitive.

entry.title: Adapting video diffusion transformers to track the same object across views and time
entry.summary: Repurposing Video Diffusion Transformers for Cross-View Temporal Object Correspondence arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper introduces XTrack, a framework that keeps the identity of an object consistent across different camera views and over time, starting from a query mask. It repurposes a pretrained video diffusion transformer to transport RGB information into mask latents, jointly handling cross-view matching and temporal tracking. To improve reliability, it adds focal cross-view attention alignment, hard negative conditioning, and local context cropping, and it converts sparse Ego-Exo4D annotations into dense pseudo-labels for training.

entry.title: Know, Then Draw: A New Training Approach for Visual Generation
entry.summary: Know, then Draw: A New Learning Paradigm for Visual Generation arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes a learning paradigm that uses autoregressive pretraining to acquire semantic knowledge and diffusion post-training for high-fidelity rendering. Controlled comparisons find autoregression to be the stronger pretraining objective for downstream rendering, and it introduces a purely semantic tokenizer trained with language supervision alone. The authors establish compute-optimal scaling laws for both stages and train a 3B-parameter text-to-image model that scores 86 on GenEval and 87 on DPG-Bench. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes a knowledge-then-rendering paradigm: autoregressive pretraining for semantics, diffusion post-training for rendering. entry.title: Rare, Relevant, Yet Still Wrong: How Memory Causes Errors in LLM Group Decisions
entry.summary: Rare, Relevant, and Still Wrong: How Memory Fails LLM Group Decisions arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper examines what a short memory should keep when an LLM group's discussion is compressed for a final decision maker. The authors introduce CrossProfile, a diagnostic benchmark of 480 tasks with automatically verified answers, to test two common heuristics: keeping the rarest facts or the facts most relevant to the decision criteria. Both heuristics fail in predictable ways, and accuracy depends more on the balance of evidence kept than on the selection policy used.

entry.title: Perceiving and predicting fast sports from a player's-eye camera using vision models
entry.summary: Perceiving and Predicting Dynamic Sports: Spatiotemporal Intelligence in Vision Models for Egocentric Tennis Video arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces an annotated tennis dataset combining egocentric video, synchronized allocentric videos, player positions, contact times, and stroke labels. The authors evaluate vision encoders, video encoders, and vision-language models on seven tasks, including localizing players and the ball, forecasting trajectories, and predicting stroke type and time to contact. They also propose a conditional diffusion model that generates whole-body tennis motion in real time from the vision predictions.

entry.title: VideoLVR: Latent Visual Reasoning over Grounded Video Evidence
entry.summary: VideoLVR: Latent Visual Reasoning over Grounded Video Evidence arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces VideoLVR, which helps multimodal large language models reason about videos by building latent visual evidence from local regions at relevant moments. This supports intermediate reasoning steps without relying only on textual coordinates or adding many cropped frames to the context. A visual token prediction objective unifies visual evidence reconstruction with text generation, and the approach is extended to reinforcement learning using final-answer rewards. Experiments on multiple video benchmarks show its effectiveness, especially for tasks needing fine-grained visual evidence.

entry.title: EnvSched: Environment-Aware Scheduling for Efficient Agent Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary: EnvSched: Environment-Aware Scheduling for Rollout-Efficient Agent Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces EnvSched, an online scheduler that decides which environment-task pairs to use in each training batch for agentic reinforcement learning, based on past rollout history. It builds a dual-relation graph that propagates statistics to predict within-task reward variance, and balances selecting high-variance tasks with covering under-observed environments. In experiments on Qwen3-8B, EnvSched reaches an average score of 48.81 across BFCL-v3, tau-Bench, and ACEBench-Agent after 40 training steps, surpassing the best score random task selection reached after 120 steps.

entry.title: Beyond Answer Changes: Matched Same-Class Controls for Audio Evidence
entry.summary: Beyond Answer Changes: Matched Same-Class Controls for Local Audio Evidence arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper examines how audio-language models respond to local edits of a queried sound event. It compares same-class and different-class replacements that share the same interval, level estimate, donor fitting, and crossfade, with only same-class replacements preserving the correct answer. Evaluated on 600 synthetic soundscapes and three models from two architecture families, the study reports how often answers change under each replacement type.

entry.title: MoI-Bench: A Benchmark for Image Generation and Editing on Phones
entry.summary: MoI-Bench: A Benchmark for Image Generation and Editing on Mobile Devices arXiv · Oct 28, 2026MoI-Bench is a benchmark for image generation and editing on mobile devices, built from mobile user needs and containing 64 subtasks and 1150 samples. It combines 16 operations with eight visual target categories and introduces MoI-Eval, a task-specific evaluation method. The authors also propose a two-dimensional Quality-Deployability map, which finds that on-device models can generate or edit efficiently but need broader task coverage and better editing quality, especially identity preservation and text rendering.

entry.title: GAS-PFN: Graph-Aware Zero-Shot Traffic Forecasting Model
entry.summary: GAS-PFN: Graph-Aware Spatiotemporal Prior-Data Fitted Networks for Zero-Shot Traffic Forecasting arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces GAS-PFN, a zero-shot model for traffic forecasting that incorporates road network topology into its synthetic training priors using random-walk diffusion. Its inference architecture uses two mask-conditioned passes through a shared Transformer to model sensor-specific temporal dynamics and interactions among neighboring sensors. Across six benchmarks at a 90-minute horizon, it reduces MSE by 34.0% on average relative to TimePFN and by 27.7% relative to four recent general-purpose zero-shot forecasters.

entry.title: TANDEM: Balancing Centralized and Decentralized Critics for the Information Gap in Multi-Agent Learning
entry.summary: TANDEM: Balancing Centralized and Decentralized Critics to Address the Information Gap in Complex Multi-Agent Environments arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper addresses the information gap in cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning under centralized training with decentralized execution, where critics see global state during training but agents lack it when acting. It proposes TANDEM, which reads one centralized critic in both a centralized and a decentralized way at each training step, uses a parameter-free gate to train on the decentralized read where the two agree, and adds a shared target to align them. The method is tested on discovery, sampling, and wildfire suppression tasks, measuring return after the centralized critic is removed. TANDEM is reported as the best method on eight of nine setups.

entry.title: A paper on the limits of latent world models, which learn internal predictive models of environments.
entry.summary: Understanding the limits of latent world models arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper examines whether latent world models, which agents use to reason over long horizons, actually capture the true dynamics of their environments. It introduces faithful latent world models as an equivariance condition between the environment's transition map and learned latent dynamics, and proposes latent rollout consistency (LRC) as a metric for evaluating action-conditioned latent prediction. The authors find that none of the state-of-the-art latent world models studied solves the task by faithfully modeling the environment's dynamics.

entry.title: Timestral: A Family of Time Series Foundation Models for Probabilistic Forecasting
entry.summary: Timestral arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces Timestral, four time series foundation models with 5M to 209M parameters for probabilistic forecasting. The authors report state-of-the-art results on GIFT-Eval, TIME, and fev-bench, with the 209M and 123M models taking the top two places on every metric. The approach combines Decoupled Horizon Forecasting, a covariate framework supporting known-future covariates in a causal architecture, and a two-stage pipeline of synthetic-data pretraining followed by post-training on mixed real and synthetic data with extended context. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes decoupled horizon forecasting (DHF) and four models from 5M to 209M parameters, reporting state-of-the-art results on GIFT-Eval, TIME, and fev-bench, with the two largest models taking the to

entry.title: REGER: A Generative Recommendation Framework Modeling Item Relations via Semantic IDs
entry.summary: REGER: Modeling inter-item Relations with Semantic IDs for Generative Recommendation arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes REGER, a framework for generative recommendation that explicitly incorporates inter-item semantic and collaborative relations into semantic pretraining, history encoding, and semantic ID generation. It provides a theoretical analysis of hierarchical preference decomposition over the SID prefix tree and distills a discriminative teacher's conditional distributions alongside cross-entropy training. Experiments on real-world datasets are reported to show consistent improvements over existing generative recommendation baselines.

entry.title: Zero-shot detection of events in soccer broadcasts without special training
entry.summary: Zero-Shot Multimodal Event Spotting in Soccer Broadcasts arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents a zero-shot framework that detects, classifies, and temporally locates events in full-length soccer broadcasts without training task-specific parameters. Matches are split into overlapping clips, each represented by a compact visual storyboard and aligned commentary transcript, processed jointly by a general-purpose multimodal model. On three manually annotated matches with 130 events, the best configuration reaches 72.0% F1@5s and outperforms SoccerNet-trained CALF and NetVLAD++ in a cross-dataset setting.

entry.title: Spectral Braids: A Topological Descriptor for Dynamic Directed Networks
entry.summary: Spectral Braids: A Topological Descriptor for Dynamic Directed Networks arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes spectral braids, a method for learning from dynamic directed networks. Each network snapshot is reduced to a community-level transition matrix, its complex eigenvalues are tracked over time, and the resulting braid is encoded as a word and mapped by the Burau representation to a fixed-size feature vector. On synthetic online-community networks, the features reach 97.1% accuracy on four classes, compared with 44.5% for the best feature set that does not track eigenvalues.

entry.title: Identifying Film Characters by Watching the Movie Like a Human
entry.summary: As the Story Unfolds: Watching a Film and Identifying Characters as a Human Does arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper addresses identifying principal characters and assigning their names using only the movie itself, without external cast lists or pre-built character banks. The authors define a character naming task, where a name mentioned in dialogue must be matched to the visible character using video context. They provide a dataset with annotations, a video-and-dialogue model, and a progressive framework for building a character bank as the film unfolds.

entry.title: The Noise Plane: A Diffusion Bridge Across Exponent and Dispersion
entry.summary: The Noise Plane: A Diffusion Bridge Across Exponent and Dispersion arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes p-Bridge, a unified diffusion framework for denoising Tweedie-distributed sensor noise. An exponent p describes how noise variance relates to intensity, and accumulated measurement controls the noise level, together spanning Gaussian, Poisson, and Gamma models. A single exponent-conditioned network handles different noise exponents without separate training. Experiments on synthetic images, fluorescence microscopy, and SAR images show its effectiveness.

entry.title: LCM-Promo: An LLM-Based Uplift Model for Promotion Allocation
entry.summary: LCM-Promo: An LLM-Based Uplift Model for Promotion Allocation arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents LCM-Promo, an uplift model for allocating promotions that is built on a large language model. It is a task-specific Large Commerce Model, finetuned on transactional commerce data to predict user intent and response to promotions. The model learns monotonic promotion-response curves from production logs and conditions on session context such as day and delivery shift. In a production A/B test on churn reactivation, it increased conversion by 1% and reduced promotion cost by 6% compared with the Segment-EMA production baseline.

entry.title: Gym-Anything-RT: Scaling Real-Time Test Environments for Vision-Language AI Agents
entry.summary: Gym-Anything-RT: Scaling Real-Time Environments for Vision-Language Agents arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces Gym-Anything-RT, a framework for testing how well vision-language AI agents handle real-time interaction. An agentic pipeline automatically generates 100 visual minigames based on a taxonomy of six real-time capabilities. The agents perform poorly in real time, with GPT-6 Astra (xHigh) passing only 9.0% of minigames, rising to 75.0% when the environment is paused. The authors have publicly released the framework and the generated minigames.

entry.title: ReferStream: Interactive Subject Injection for Streaming Video Generation
entry.summary: ReferStream: Interactive Subject Injection for Streaming Video Generation arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents ReferStream, a framework that adds new visual subjects to a video while it is being generated, without any extra training. It combines Joint Latent, which places reference latents into the current scene so their features are extracted in context, with Cache Restoration, which uses these features for the injection chunk and then restores overwritten cache entries. The authors also introduce ReferStream Bench, a benchmark with scheduled reference arrivals and subject-presence annotations. On this benchmark, ReferStream scores higher than the compared baselines, including offline methods, on text adherence, subject similarity, and count accuracy.

entry.title: Pneuma: A Real-World Benchmark for Predicting Commercial Aircraft Maintenance Needs
entry.summary: Pneuma: A Large-Scale Real-World Time Series Benchmark for Commercial Aircraft Predictive Maintenance arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces Pneuma, a publicly available benchmark for predictive maintenance built from onboard time series data of in-service commercial aircraft. It centers on bleed air systems and covers four aircraft types and nine verified fault scenarios aligned with real maintenance logs. The benchmark defines three tasks: multivariate forecasting, supervised fault classification, and unsupervised anomaly detection. Evaluating over 25 models, the authors find that even strong current models struggle to detect subtle fault signatures.

entry.title: When uncertainty measures fail: fixing biased deferral in imbalanced clinical prediction
entry.summary: When uncertainty quantification fails: structural vulnerabilities and corrections for selective prediction under clinical class imbalance arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies selective prediction in clinical AI, where high-confidence cases are decided automatically and ambiguous cases are deferred to human experts. It finds that in prognostic tasks with severe class imbalance, standard uncertainty scores can reflect class membership rather than clinical ambiguity, systematically penalizing minority patients. The authors propose a corrective framework, tested across 56 synthetic conditions and three neurodegenerative cohorts. They recommend threshold-aligned uncertainty measures and class-stratified evaluation.

entry.title: How Models Collapse When Self-Rewarding Across Many Problems in Label-Free RL
entry.summary: Collective Dynamics of Self-Reinforcement: How Cross-Task Coupling Drives Policy Collapse in Unsupervised RLVR arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper studies label-free reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), where a language model is rewarded for agreeing with its own majority vote. Reasoning first improves but eventually collapses, sometimes to the same answer for every problem. The authors explain the dependence on dataset size as a collective instability in a model where problems share parameters, deriving a critical number of problems above which collapse occurs. Simulations and experiments with a small Transformer support these predictions.

entry.title: Judging Articulated Object Manipulation by Joint Constraints
entry.summary: Kinematic Constraint-Referenced Evaluation for Articulated Object Manipulation arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper argues that manipulation policies are usually judged only by binary task success, which cannot show whether a commanded motion matches the object's kinematic constraints. The authors propose Constraint-Referenced Strategy (CRS), which projects the commanded end-effector twist onto the object's joint axis to separate progress along the joint from off-constraint motion. CRS requires a joint model and a joint-following scripted controller derived from it, but no recorded demonstrations or learned judge.

entry.title: When, Where, and What to Correct: Human-Guided Robot Policy Refinement
entry.summary: When, Where, and What to Correct: Human-Guided Adaptive Residual Correction for Robot Policies arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces Adaptive Residual Correction (ARC), a lightweight post-training module that learns a residual correction on top of a frozen robot policy using reinforcement learning. Sparse human corrections guide autonomous exploration by determining when residual control activates and where in the residual action space refinement should explore, while task reward determines the final residual executed. On three precision-manipulation tasks on a real robot, ARC raised average task success from 33.3% to 75.0%.

entry.title: GroundControl: Generating new views of outdoor scenes from street and satellite images without 3D reconstruction
entry.summary: GroundControl: Satellite-Conditioned Multi-View Diffusion for Reconstruction-Free Novel View Synthesis arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes a multi-view diffusion model that synthesizes novel views of outdoor scenes by conditioning on both satellite images and street-level input images. It uses cross-attention conditioning to keep pretrained multi-view diffusion priors while following the scene layout shown in the satellite views, and it does not rely on 3D scene reconstruction. Experiments on outdoor datasets report better novel-view synthesis than satellite-only or street-view-only baselines, especially when target and source views overlap very little.

entry.title: Which Hand Was Late? Diagnosing Robot Failures in Two-Handed Tool Use
entry.summary: Which Hand Was Late? Diagnosis for Robot Failure Recovery in Bimanual Tool Use arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies how a robot can diagnose failures in bimanual tool-use tasks, where a tool may slip or one hand may act late. Using a simulated task whose failure causes are read from recorded traces, the authors compare what different sensing channels reveal about these causes. They find that a repair policy that escalates when the cause cannot be identified repairs about as many failures within two attempts as one given the true cause.

entry.title: GTFormer: A Linear-Time Graph Network Alternative to Transformer Self-Attention
entry.summary: GTFormer: A Syntax-Free Graph Network Alternative to Transformers for 8192× Length Extrapolation in Linear Time arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes GTFormer, a hierarchical graph neural network that replaces the all-to-all self-attention of Transformers for long-sequence modeling. It is trained only on sequences of 512 tokens or fewer and evaluated on eight long-context benchmarks. The authors report zero-shot extrapolation to 4,194,304 tokens (8192 times the training length) on one commodity GPU with linear memory use, while keeping near-perfect accuracy.

entry.title: The Structure Gap: Why More Data Cannot Replace Structured Reasoning
entry.summary: The Structure Gap: When More Data Cannot Replace Structured Reasoning arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper examines the belief that large learners trained on enough data can make explicit domain knowledge unnecessary. It defines structure-encoded problems, whose input-output maps are determined by known structures such as solvers, symmetry groups, graphs, or physical laws, and introduces the "structure gap" between methods that receive this structure and learners that receive only examples. The authors prove results for a Gaussian inverse problem and support the mechanisms with controlled experiments on known-operator inversion, sparse recovery, and graph reachability.

entry.title: Orthogonal, parameterized steering of LLMs across several traits at once
entry.summary: Orthogonal and Parametrized Multi-Attribute Steering of LLMs arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies how to steer large language model behavior at inference time using activation steering. It first identifies the most steerable interval for each steering vector and rescales the steering range accordingly. It then introduces parameterized steering, which sets activations to a desired trait strength instead of pushing them in a direction. To handle interference when combining several traits, the authors orthogonalize the steering vectors so that traits are decoupled and multiple behaviors can be steered simultaneously.

entry.title: A study on data-efficient fine-tuning of vision foundation models
entry.summary: A note on data-efficient finetuning of vision foundation models arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents an empirical evaluation of how vision foundation models are efficiently adapted to new tasks. It compares attention-, convolution-, and Mamba-based model families across transfer methods including visual prompting, linear probing, full fine-tuning, and LoRA. The authors also examine whether common regularization techniques can improve visual prompting performance, aiming to offer practical guidelines under limited resources.
