entry.title: Grounding LLM agents in business processes using process-aware knowledge graphs
entry.summary: Grounding LLM Agents in Business Processes: Process-Aware Knowledge Graphs for Reliable Multi-Step Service Invocation arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper integrates OData metadata and BPMN reference processes into a typed property graph, with a hybrid retriever that follows process edges to find subsequent endpoints. On 42 enterprise services, it improves Recall@3 for queries with low lexical overlap with downstream entities. On 81 multi-step queries, an LLM agent completes 38.7% of tasks versus 10.3% for a chunk-based baseline.

entry.title: Decision Models as Judges for Hallucination Detection
entry.summary: Decision Models as Judges for Hallucination Detection arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper tests whether cheaper decision models, which output fixed verdicts with probabilities, can replace generative large language models as judges for detecting hallucinations. The authors built binary benchmarks for five hallucination types, with 9,852 items from six datasets, and compared five decision models with the generative judge gpt-6-sol. Performance varies by type: the best decision model matches the generative judge on context inconsistency but trails it on logical and instruction inconsistency.

entry.title: Using Nineteenth-Century Editions to Aid Recognition of a Thirteenth-Century Papal Register
entry.summary: Mining the Nineteenth Century for the Thirteenth: Register-Scale Forced Alignment and HTR Bootstrapping via Legacy Regesta and Antiquarian Editions arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper examines how nineteenth-century regesta and partial editions can support handwritten text recognition of the registers of Pope Honorius III. Using the regnal years with existing modern transcriptions as a benchmark, the authors test what this legacy material contributes at the orthographic, lexical, and topological levels. They conclude that such editions cannot replace modern transcription but can guide, check, and segment recognition across untranscribed registers.

entry.title: TrawMem: Task-Oriented Role-Adaptive Memory Workspaces for AI Agents
entry.summary: TrawMem: Reframing Agent Memory as Task-Oriented Role-Adaptive Workspaces arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper argues that current memory systems for large language model agents retrieve memories by relevance to the current query, which does not capture how each memory helps solve a task. The authors propose TrawMem, which organizes interaction histories into local threads and builds task-oriented workspaces by assigning roles to memories and jointly selecting complementary ones. Experiments on LoCoMo and MemGallery with four backbone models show consistent gains over representative memory systems in macro-F1.

entry.title: AdaGround: A training-free method that adaptively zooms and verifies clicks to locate GUI elements on screens
entry.summary: AdaGround: Token-Normalized Adaptive Zooming with Verifier-in-the-Loop Refinement for GUI Grounding arXiv · Oct 27, 2026AdaGround is a training-free framework for locating interface elements on high-resolution screens, especially small targets. It adjusts zoom settings based on the model's own estimate of target size, and uses a Yes/No verifier with marked clicks to keep or reject zooms and trigger re-grounding. It also composes spreadsheet cells from their headers. On Qwen3-VL models, it outperforms existing training-free zooming methods and many trained GUI models, and its gains extend to the held-out UI-Vision benchmark.

entry.title: WithinVAE: A compact image autoencoder that learns meaning without borrowed recognition models
entry.summary: WithinVAE: Compact Visual Autoencoding with Self-Distilled Semantics arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper introduces WithinVAE, a compact variational visual autoencoder that learns semantic structure through self-distillation from an exponential-moving-average copy of itself, rather than from a pretrained recognition encoder. It uses a sequential bottleneck and position-dependent token masking to achieve 4-fold compression. On ImageNet-1K at 256×256, it improves all four reconstruction metrics over RPiAE, including a 1.36 dB PSNR gain, with half the latent capacity. Under frozen evaluation, its linear probing accuracy exceeds RPiAE by 6.5 points and the reconstruction-only baseline by 5.1 points, which the authors attribute to self-distillation.

entry.title: Locating Causal Attention Heads for Evidence Effects in Transformers
entry.summary: Causal Localization of Evidence Effects in Transformers arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper introduces controlled evidence aggregation, which varies symbol counts and order in prompts to measure a frozen Transformer's preference between two answer tokens. A selection method called BUC identifies compact sets of attention heads whose ablation removes 65.5-91.6% of the count effect in Pythia-410M. Eight heads chosen only on symbolic prompts also lower mean accuracy by 8.2 points on a natural language evidence task, compared with 0.8 points for random matched sets.

entry.title: Physical structure as an organizing principle for universal Hamiltonian learning
entry.summary: Physical structure as an organizing principle for universal Hamiltonian learning arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper introduces UniTB, a universal E(3) equivariant framework that combines density-functional tight-binding physics with deep learning to predict electronic Hamiltonians across many chemistries. Trained on 29,242 crystals, it reaches a 0.48 meV matrix-element error on nonmagnetic test crystals spanning 68 elements. A faster variant, UniTB-Flash, is also presented, and both models are used to screen 16,195 crystals.

entry.title: Strategyproof deep reinforcement learning for allocating online resources
entry.summary: Strategyproof Deep Reinforcement Learning for Online Resource Allocation arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper addresses two linked problems in online resource allocation: distributing scarce resources efficiently under uncertain future demand, and ensuring agents report task values and requirements truthfully. The authors introduce the first strategyproof deep reinforcement learning mechanism for this setting, combining a monotonic neural network, a generalised critical payment, and training by either RL or imitation of an existing rule. In experiments on a four-resource stream, the neural rule achieves 97.8% of an offline welfare upper bound, and imitation reaches 97.5% in 261 seconds, about 89 times faster than RL.

entry.title: ALADDIN: One-Step Face Swapping via Adversarial Latent Diffusion Distillation
entry.summary: ALADDIN: Adversarial Latent Diffusion Distillation for One-Step Identity Swapping arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents ALADDIN, a one-step face-swapping method that transfers a source identity onto a target image while keeping the target's pose, expression, hair, and lighting. The generator is initialised from a pre-trained multi-step flow-matching model and trained adversarially under identity and target-preservation constraints. The authors report that it is state-of-the-art among one-step methods in realism and target preservation at comparable identity transfer, and matches the best multi-step model with 28 times fewer network evaluations.

entry.title: Regression functions as fields over covariates: evolution equations and identification
entry.summary: Regression Functions as Fields on Covariate Space: Evolution Equations, the Hessian, and Identification arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper treats the conditional mean of an outcome given covariates at each time as a field over covariate space and studies how it evolves when covariates and outcomes change over time. It shows this field satisfies a second-order evolution equation whose diffusion term is the trace of the regression Hessian weighted by the covariate covariance. The authors also connect the Hessian to quadratic regression and kernel smoother bias, and show that for binary outcomes the equation reduces to a Nagumo-type equation with logistic travelling fronts.

entry.title: semanticfa: An R package for analyzing psychological scale structure from item meanings without response data
entry.summary: semanticfa: An R Package for Response-Free Semantic Factor Analysis of Psychometric Scales arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper introduces semanticfa, an R package that performs factor analysis on similarities between language-model embeddings of psychometric scale items, without needing respondent data. A worked example applies it to the 50-item IPIP Big-Five markers embedded with Qwen3-Embedding-8B and compares the results with a factor analysis of 874,434 respondents. The authors propose semantic-behavioral coherence, the agreement between semantic and response structures, as a measurable scale property, and argue that semantic factor analysis complements rather than replaces response-based analysis.

entry.title: Teaching ecological reality to AI: a plug-in training corpus for living-system welfare
entry.summary: Teach reality, not ethics: a drop-in continued-pretraining corpus installs coupled human-biosphere-AI welfare dispositions across model families arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper argues that large language models increasingly make decisions affecting living systems, yet ecological reasoning is rarely a focus of training. The authors built a real-data continued-pretraining corpus covering human, biosphere and AI dependencies, option value under irreversibility, and recovery from harm. Installed on five open models, it reduced harmful choices under the highest pressure to zero or near zero in four of them, with MMLU unchanged. A construct-neutral control corpus showed no such improvement.

entry.title: From Interaction to Capability: Task Advancement as State and Supervision for GUI Agents
entry.summary: From Interaction to Capability: Task Advancement as State and Supervision for GUI Agents arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces Task Advancement Memory (TAM), which treats verified task progress as the core mechanism for GUI agents, letting them build on earlier results across applications in long workflows and learn reusable operations. On MobileWorld GUI-only tasks, Advancement State alone raises success from 12.0% to 28.2%, and full TAM achieves a 17.6% relative gain over the strongest baseline while cutting lifecycle tokens per solved task by 38.7%. On SPA-Bench's single-app English Level 3 setting, TAM reaches state-of-the-art task success.

entry.title: Following Gradients to Find Training Data That Erodes Model Safety
entry.summary: Follow the Gradient: Tracing Safety Degradation Back to Training Data arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper shows that fine-tuning large language models on instruction data can weaken their safety even when individual examples look harmless. It introduces SimpleLoRIF, a scalable gradient embedding method that identifies training examples whose gradients align with unsafe behavior. Using it, the authors build SafeTulu by removing the 20% of Tulu 3 examples most aligned with unsafe responses, which reduces GCG attack success rate by up to 22% across Qwen, Llama, and Olmo while largely preserving capability. ★★★★ Notable: The authors simplify low-rank gradient attribution to filter million-example fine-tuning sets for safety-degrading data; the abstract reports up to 22% lower GCG attack success across Qwen, Llama, and

entry.title: Running Activity Recognition Inside the Radio: A Spiking Accelerator for mmWave Sensing
entry.summary: Keeping Inference in the Radio: Design and Measurement of a Spiking Accelerator for mmWave ISAC Activity Recognition arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies whether spiking neural networks can recognize human activity from mmWave integrated sensing and communication channel estimates while remaining powered when the main processors sleep. The authors implement SNN accelerators with a spike encoder on a ZCU208 RFSoC, so the full chain from micro-Doppler frame to activity label runs in programmable logic. A 132-neuron fully connected SNN reaches 94.7% accuracy on unseen subjects of the DISC dataset with 206 microsecond inference. Compared with conventional networks of the same topology, it uses one-eighth the logic and less dynamic energy per decision.

entry.title: HGPRGDel: A Learning and Ranking Method for Growth-Coupled Gene Deletion Design
entry.summary: HGPRGDel: GPR-Aware Learning and Ranking for Growth-Coupled Gene Deletion Design arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents a reusable protocol for designing microbial strains in which cell growth is coupled to production of a target compound. It learns from previously computed gene-deletion strategies to rank gene-deletion priorities for each target metabolite, then evaluates candidate strategies with constraint-based metabolic analysis. The learning component, HGPRGDel, explicitly models gene-protein-reaction logic and achieves the highest macro-F1 and AUC among the evaluated configurations on e_coli_core, iMM904, and iML1515. Its rankings recovered an average of 90% of the reference deletion genes from MetNetComp while examining fewer genes than the baseline methods.

entry.title: QD-PINN: Neural-network method for Bayesian quickest detection in high-dimensional diffusions
entry.summary: QD-PINN:A Physics-Informed Neural Network Approach to Bayesian Quickest Detection in High-Dimensional Diffusions arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper proposes a physics-informed neural network framework for estimating optimal stopping boundaries in quickest detection problems with high-dimensional diffusion processes. It establishes an equivalence between the free-boundary PDE and an infinite-dimensional stochastic optimization problem to justify using finite-dimensional networks. Uncertainty in the learned boundaries is quantified with deep ensembles and Monte Carlo dropout, showing low variability, and results closely match reference numerical solutions where available.

entry.title: How reliable are individual brain-network attributions in ADNI resting-state fMRI cognitive prediction?
entry.summary: How Reliable Is Individualized Functional-Network Attribution in Resting-State fMRI Cognitive Prediction in ADNI? arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper examines whether per-subject attributions of which functional brain networks drive a resting-state fMRI cognitive prediction model are reliable. Using 875 subjects from ADNI, it predicts MMSE and ADAS-Cog13 from Schaefer-200 functional connectivity. Split-half reliability is near ceiling but falls on scan-rescan retests, and matched pairs exceed a mismatched-subject permutation null. The authors conclude attributions carry a modest person-specific component on top of a strong population-shared pattern.

entry.title: PerceptRL: Making Visual Perception Rewardable in Multimodal LLMs
entry.summary: PerceptRL: Making Visual Perception Rewardable in MLLMs from Answers to Interactions arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper addresses the weakness of fine-grained visual perception in multimodal large language models after post-training. PerceptRL uses a multi-agent pipeline to turn verified errors from dense image captions into QA pairs with rule-based rewards, and adds multi-turn reinforcement learning with visual tools. Coordinate Injection and a grounding-aware process reward correct spatial drift during tool use. Across seven benchmarks, the method reaches 71.6% average accuracy.

entry.title: Reinforcement-learning control for autonomous fixed-wing drone interception
entry.summary: Autonomous fixed-wing interception using reinforcement learning arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper presents a fixed-wing interceptor drone controlled by a neural network that maps filtered monocular vision observations directly to actuator commands. The policy was trained in a custom Python environment using reinforcement learning with proximal policy optimization, then deployed on a fixed-wing platform. In simulation it outperformed two classical guidance controllers under most conditions, and it successfully intercepted maneuvering fixed-wing targets in real flight.

entry.title: Whether later model releases keep earlier pretraining disclosure: a document audit of 41 language model entries
entry.summary: What Carries Forward? Pretraining Disclosure Across Language Model Releases arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper audits 41 language model entries from 17 families using 24 pretraining-related indicators from the 2025 Foundation Model Transparency Index. It compares adjacent releases across ten families, tracking which disclosures were gained, lost, or retained. The authors find that scores more often fall than rise, with more indicator losses than gains, and that unchanged or higher totals can hide lost disclosures.

entry.title: Concordat: a Python library that enforces step-by-step rules on LLM agents at run time
entry.summary: Concordat: Typed Sessions for LLM Agents arXiv · Oct 28, 2026Concordat is an open-source Python library that models an LLM agent's allowed behaviour as a finite-state protocol enforced during execution. On each turn the model sees only the tools legal in its current state, and illegal calls are rejected before side effects occur. In an evaluation on 50 tau-bench airline tasks with simulated customers pressing for skipped confirmations, the standard agent made unconfirmed changes in several tasks while the Concordat agent made none, with no significant difference in task success. ★★★★ Notable: Applies session types and typestate to enforce protocols on LLM agents at runtime, offering only state-legal tools and rejecting out-of-protocol calls before side effects. The authors report that stan

entry.title: M4Bench: A Benchmark for Procedural Specs in EHR Derivation Agents
entry.summary: M4Bench: Evaluating Procedural Specification for Clinical EHR Derivation Agents arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces M4Bench, a benchmark of 28 clinical variable derivation tasks across 15 task families on MIMIC-IV and eICU. It tests whether AI coding agents can reproduce these derivations and how clinician-reviewed agent skills affect their results. Skills raised reward by 0.136 on average, mostly due to specification completeness, while only a few runs passed every strict check. The tasks, skills, evaluation code, and run evidence are released as open source. ★★★★ Notable: Introduces M4Bench for clinical EHR derivation and reports that specification completeness, not the skill format, accounts for most of the gain for AI coding agents, though few runs fully pass strict

entry.title: Input Skip Reparameterizes a VAE Without Necessarily Improving Its Generator
entry.summary: An Input Skip Can Reparameterize a VAE Without Improving the Generator arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper shows that adding a constant input skip to a Gaussian variational autoencoder can be rewritten so that the distribution of generated samples stays unchanged while reconstruction mean squared error shrinks by a fixed factor. Experiments on a Gaussian case with known density and on seven DART tsunami records find that lower reconstruction error does not reliably improve energy score. The authors conclude that assessing generation requires measures beyond reconstruction error.

entry.title: Interpretable Meta-Policies for Neural Decision Making: a hierarchical RL framework that puts transparent reasoning in high-level skills
entry.summary: Interpretable Meta-Policies for Neural Decision Making arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents NEXUS, a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework that combines neural skills with symbolic meta-policies. By moving transparent reasoning to high-level skills rather than atomic actions, it greatly reduces symbolic complexity without sacrificing environment performance. The authors also compare neural, symbolic, and neuro-symbolic meta-policy architectures in terms of environmental return and aligned task performance.

entry.title: Graph Representation Learning via Adaptive Expectile Aggregation: a learnable expectile level replaces simple averaging to capture more neighborhood information.
entry.summary: Graph Representation Learning via Adaptive Expectile Aggregation arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper proposes ExpectileGCN, an adaptive graph aggregation framework that uses a learnable expectile level to capture neighborhood information beyond the mean. The operator moves continuously between minimum- and maximum-type behavior, with mean aggregation as a special case, and is made differentiable through sigmoid smoothing and fixed-point iterations. The authors provide stability and transductive generalization guarantees and analyze classification risk under heterophilic neighborhood models. Experiments on homophilic and heterophilic benchmark graphs show strong predictive performance and improved robustness under feature corruption and structural perturbations.

entry.title: ETAMem: A Memory Framework for Long-Term Chatbot Conversations
entry.summary: ETAMem: Decoupling and Aligning Heterogeneous Memory for Long-Term Conversational Agents arXiv · Oct 28, 2026ETAMem is a multi-view memory framework for long-term conversational agents built on large language models. It breaks conversation information into atomic memory units, identifies affective content, and organizes these units into three complementary views: Event, Affect, and Time. Retrieval allocates budgets across views based on each query. On the LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S benchmarks, it reports relative accuracy gains of 12.46% and 7.96% over state-of-the-art baselines.

entry.title: CRISP: Co-designing Pruning and Scheduling for Efficient MoE Inference on Edge Servers
entry.summary: CRISP: Co-designing Pruning and Scheduling for Efficient MoE Inference on Edge Servers arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper addresses efficient inference for Mixture-of-Experts models on memory-constrained edge devices, where moving expert weights dominates latency. It proposes CRISP, which reorders neurons by importance so one stored expert supports multiple execution widths, and assigns differentiated execution to hot, warm, and cold expert combinations based on frequency and expert role. Evaluated on Mixtral-8x7B and DeepSeek-MoE-16B, CRISP improves throughput by up to 2.1 times at the same memory budget, with accuracy loss limited to 3.6% relative to full-width inference.

entry.title: Rethinking Visual Imagination for Spatial Reasoning: Representing Unseen States Beyond RGB
entry.summary: Representing the Unseen: Rethinking Visual Imagination for Spatial Reasoning arXiv · Oct 28, 2026Visual world models often generate RGB views of unobserved states to support spatial reasoning, though RGB is mainly the default because it suits visual generation. The authors introduce ImagiRep, a simulator-grounded benchmark of 922 questions across seven types and two settings, offering RGB and six alternative representations such as depth, panoramas, and top-down geometry. They find that accurate imagined RGB does not ensure accurate reasoning, and different questions benefit from different representations. They also propose GEARS, a lightweight test-time method for adaptive representation selection, which outperforms existing spatial imagination methods.

entry.title: FeatureArc: Testing Coding Agents on Features That Grow Over Time
entry.summary: FeatureArc: Benchmarking Coding Agents on Evolving Features arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces FeatureArc, a benchmark that evaluates coding agents on software features that evolve through successive stages, with each extension building on the agent's own earlier code. Tasks are built from repository histories and checked with executable tests across four programming languages. Evaluating 10 agents on 73 tasks, pooled success falls from 62.7% at the first stage to 28.5% on the whole feature. Inherited defects from earlier stages are a common cause of failure. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose FeatureArc, a benchmark and pipeline for evolving features; across 10 agents and 73 tasks, pooled success falls from 62.7% at the first stage to 28.5% for the whole feature.

entry.title: Confidence Scoring for Segmentation in Any CNN
entry.summary: Segmentation Confidence for Arbitrary CNNs arXiv · Oct 28, 2026Convolutional neural networks are widely used for medical image segmentation but lack a built-in confidence measure. This study explores voxel-based uncertainty estimation methods that can be added to existing segmentation pipelines without training from scratch. It also proposes a new method for deriving a single confidence score from uncertainty maps, and evaluations on different regions of interest and modalities suggest this score can predict segmentation performance on unseen data.

entry.title: How instructions, post-training, and internal activations affect whether multimodal models refuse questions a picture cannot answer
entry.summary: When Visual Evidence Is Insufficient: How Instructions, Post-Training, and Internal Activations Shape Refusal in Multimodal Language Models arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies whether multimodal language models refuse to answer questions that an image cannot support. Across three models on the MoHoBench benchmark, the authors compare inference-time instructions, supervised and preference-based post-training, and interventions on a refusal-related activation direction. Refusal is sensitive to how instructions are worded and placed, post-training raises refusal more strongly, and activation interventions produce smaller changes that transfer across prompt conditions.

entry.title: Adaptive rollout allocation to improve GRPO training for LLMs
entry.summary: Bayes-Adaptive MDPs for Rollout Allocation to Enhance GRPO Training arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper notes that GRPO gives every training question the same rollout budget, ignoring differences in difficulty. It proposes AdaRoll-GRPO, which models rollout allocation as a Bayes-adaptive Markov decision process to learn an adaptive allocation policy. The policy is computed offline and applied during training, under the same total rollout budget as standard GRPO. Experiments on multiple reasoning datasets and LLM architectures show improved GRPO training performance under a fixed budget.

entry.title: Shared Latent Number Geometry Across Text and Image Arithmetic
entry.summary: Beyond the Readout: A Latent Numerical Frame Shared Across Modality and Operation arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper asks whether a multimodal model uses one internal concept of number for arithmetic given as text or as an image. Using causal interventions on Gemma4-12B-it's residual stream, the authors learn subspaces where swapping coordinates changes the model's answer. The subspaces for different conditions use different directions but can be aligned by one rotation and rescaling. The study also finds hidden directions that carry the number without affecting the current output digit and that steer later digits. ★★★★ Notable: Uses causal interventions instead of similarity metrics to find text and image arithmetic share one numerical geometry, with hidden directions that don't affect the printed digit still carrying the nu

entry.title: Displacement Moments and Path-Terminal Separation in Brownian Interpolant Sampling
entry.summary: Displacement Moments and Path-Terminal Separation in Brownian Interpolant Sampling arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies sampling error in Brownian stochastic interpolants, which connect paired endpoint samples, and shows that this error can depend on displacement moments even when neither endpoint has a first moment. For arbitrary Borel couplings, the authors prove early-stopped KL guarantees from target to output for standard Euler sampling. The work also compares bridge-path, comparison-path, and terminal KL behavior, and identifies the source information lost through Markov projection.

entry.title: CTBakeGS: Converting photorealistic CT renderings into 3D Gaussian splats without training
entry.summary: CTBakeGS: training-free baking of photorealistic CT volume renderings into 3D Gaussian splats arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents CTBakeGS, a method that converts photorealistic CT volume renderings directly into 3D Gaussian splatting (3DGS) models without any training. Splats are placed on an adaptive octree of millimetre-sized cells, with colour and opacity computed on the graphics processor. Tested on six public CT scans, two-million-splat models reached PSNR values of roughly 30 to 33 dB, and conversion took seconds to about a minute on ordinary computers. The converted models rendered at 68 frames per second on a laptop.

entry.title: Clearing the FoG: training knowledge graph agents to retrieve evidence for their answers
entry.summary: Clearing the FoG: Training KG Agents to Retrieve the Evidence Behind Their Answers arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper argues that existing knowledge graph question-answering agents are trained and rewarded only for correct answers, so they often answer correctly without retrieving the supporting triples. It proposes FoG, which combines evidence-grounded question synthesis, a KG interaction agent, and an evidence-coverage process reward that credits each supporting triple to the turn that first retrieves it. On three KGQA benchmarks, 3B–4B open-source agents trained with FoG outperform substantially larger baselines in answer accuracy and evidence coverage, and transfer zero-shot to other knowledge graphs.

entry.title: An end-to-end framework for validating generative models with uncertainty
entry.summary: An end-to-end framework for uncertainty-aware validation of generative models arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper proposes SIGMA, an end-to-end framework that combines density estimation with principled uncertainty quantification. Using Gaussian mixture models, the authors profile fitting uncertainties as nuisance parameters in a composite goodness-of-fit test, rather than treating the model as exact. Experiments on a two-dimensional toy model and a collider physics QCD background benchmark show the model can be trusted on test sets up to an order of magnitude larger than standard tests allow.

entry.title: Game-theoretic agent with Bayesian opponent modeling and moral rhetoric for the GLEE competition
entry.summary: Game-Theoretic Solvers with Bayesian Opponent Modeling and Moral Rhetoric Framing for GLEE arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper describes an agent submitted to the GLEE Competition, which involves bargaining, negotiation, and persuasion games against human and AI opponents. The agent combines a classical game-theoretic solver for numeric moves, an online Bayesian layer that estimates opponent types, and a language model that writes messages. It was evaluated over 13,200 Monte Carlo games against 11 synthetic opponent archetypes and through analysis of 9,337 live-game messages. In the persuasion setting, moral rhetoric framing was strongly correlated with whether the buyer purchased, even after controlling for quality, round, and configuration.

entry.title: Learning Robot Policies Whose Execution Quality Can Be Controlled via Iterative Hindsight Relabeling
entry.summary: Learning Quality-Controllable Robot Policies with Iterative Hindsight Relabeling arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper introduces Quality-Controllable Policy (QCP), a robot policy whose execution speed, motion smoothness, and their combinations can be controlled at inference time. To expand the controllable quality range beyond the initial demonstrations, it adds an iterative loop that collects rollouts under target quality labels, relabels trajectories by their measured quality, and fine-tunes the policy. Experiments on Robomimic and RoboEval show improved execution quality and success rates across iterations, and real-world tests show gains in conveyor throughput and wine-glass transport success.

entry.title: JEPA-inspired latent field prediction for reconstructing MIMO-OFDM channels from sparse pilots
entry.summary: JEPA-Inspired Latent Field Prediction for Sparse-Pilot MIMO-OFDM Channel Reconstruction arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper addresses the high pilot overhead needed to acquire full channel state information in MIMO-OFDM wireless systems. It proposes a JEPA-inspired world model of the wireless propagation field that maps channel observations into latent time-frequency tokens and predicts masked or future latent states from historical multi-band context. The predicted prior is fused with sparse noisy current pilots to reconstruct the full channel. Ray-tracing experiments show improved normalized mean square error over pilot-only and direct reconstruction baselines.

entry.title: LinMix: Data Mixing Framed as Linear Domain Attribution
entry.summary: LinMix: Data Mixing as Linear Domain Attribution arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies how the mixture of domains in a language model's pretraining data affects performance. It proposes LinMix, which samples data mixes at the vertices of a capped simplex so each domain is at its cap or absent, yielding an interpretable linear model whose coefficients are domain attributions. In pretraining experiments with 1B and 4B parameter models, LinMix outperforms Dirichlet-based mixing on reasoning, code, and math benchmarks, and it supports linear fitting across 288 fine-grained domains. ★★★★ Notable: Recasts data mixing as linear domain attribution, replacing Dirichlet with vertex sampling; the authors give an optimality proof and report relative gains of 46% on MBPP and 14% on GSM8K over Dirichle

entry.title: How many and how much negative samples? RADAR, a contrastive learning method for knowledge graph embedding
entry.summary: How Many and How Much? Contrastive Learning with Negative Samples for Knowledge Graph Embedding arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper examines how many negative samples to use for each positive sample and how much each should contribute when training knowledge graph embeddings with contrastive learning. The authors propose RADAR, which combines risk-aware negative budget allocation with distribution-calibrated negative weighting. Experiments on 3 real-world knowledge graphs with 4 embedding models show RADAR achieves the best average performance across all combinations and reduces sampled false negatives by over 90%.

entry.title: Para-Gaussian approximations for random deep neural networks, a more accurate model of their behaviour beyond the Gaussian limit.
entry.summary: Para-Gaussian Approximations of Random Deep Neural Networks arXiv · Oct 28, 2026Randomly initialized neural networks are known to behave like Gaussians as width goes to infinity, but this approximation is poor at finite width and worsens with depth. The paper introduces a slightly non-Gaussian, more accurate approximation called the para-Gaussian distribution, built from Hermite polynomials. It gives a practical recursive method for approximating deeper layers. The theory is applied to linear networks, where results are exact, and to ReLU networks, where they are approximate.

entry.title: Calibration-free channel selection for Mixture-of-Experts decoding
entry.summary: Channel Selection for Mixture-of-Experts Decoding Needs No Calibration Data arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies how to choose which intermediate channels of Mixture-of-Experts models to read during decoding. It finds that calibrated thresholds neither fix the read budget nor reliably improve accuracy, while a top-k selection per token needs no calibration data and matches or beats threshold versions in most comparisons. The authors also propose a reader built only from the model's weights, which retains 98.1% of full-model accuracy while reading 17.8% of routed-expert weights. Triton kernels are reported to speed up MoE blocks compared with optimized vLLM.

entry.title: PDRVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Physical Dynamics Representations
entry.summary: PDRVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Physical Dynamics Representations arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents PDRVLA, a model that generates robot actions from visual observations and language instructions. A lightweight Physical Dynamics Module extracts physical tokens from vision-language features to condition actions without online video generation, reducing control-loop latency. The model reports success rates of 99.3% on LIBERO, 89.9% on LIBERO-Plus, 93.6% on RoboTwin 2.0, and 81.5% on SimplerEnv across four simulation benchmarks.

entry.title: Same Verdict, Different Readers: Tailoring Fact-Check Explanations to Individual Preferences
entry.summary: Same Verdict, Different Readers: Personalizing Fact-Checking Explanations from Relative Preferences arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies how to adapt an existing fact-checking explanation to individual readers while keeping its factual content intact. Instead of using reader-written references, the authors learn the rewriting from relative preferences of LLM-simulated readers. They propose PERPL, a framework with simulated preference construction and progressive preference learning, which discovers preferred explanations beyond predefined styles. The experiments report that PERPL outperforms much larger general-purpose LLMs on personalized preference alignment while maintaining high factual fidelity.

entry.title: Agent-Conditioned Routing for Diverse Reasoning in a Frozen Model
entry.summary: Agent-Conditioned Routing: Diverse Reasoning Paths Within One Frozen Model arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper asks whether one frozen sparse mixture-of-experts model can produce diverse solution methods for a single problem without changing its weights. The proposed Agent-Conditioned Routing assigns each parallel trajectory persistent expert-eligibility masks while keeping the learned token router. On a 126-question math and physics benchmark, it yields more problems with at least two distinct primary methods than temperature sampling, with somewhat lower correctness.

entry.title: Euclidean-crowding-driven adaptive Euclidean-hyperbolic graph learning: a paper analyzing how Euclidean and hyperbolic spaces differ on hierarchical graph data and proposing a method that fuses both geometries.
entry.summary: Euclidean Crowding-Driven Adaptive Euclidean-Hyperbolic Graph Learning arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper geometrically quantifies Euclidean crowding, showing that fixed-dimensional Euclidean embeddings of tree-like graphs suffer layer-wise minimum separation shrinkage that weakens margin-based generalization bounds. It also provides a generalization bound explaining the advantage of hyperbolic geometry on hierarchical data. The authors propose EH-Fusion, which lifts Euclidean GNN representations into hyperbolic space via exponential mapping and adaptively fuses both geometries based on node-level neighborhood expansion patterns. Experiments on benchmark datasets are reported to validate the theory and the method.

entry.title: Geometry of manifold learning: singular foliations from deep learning models
entry.summary: The Geometry of Manifold Learning: Singular foliations via Deep Learning models arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This theoretical paper studies the geometric structure a trained neural network defines on its data space, using the Data Information Matrix, a variant of the Fisher Information Matrix. The authors focus on the non-smooth case of ReLU activations, where traditional tools often fail. They prove that the distribution spanned by the matrix's columns is non-smooth in the distributional sense, and introduce a smoothed version differing only on a measure-zero set. They show this smoothed distribution induces a singular foliation on the training data space.

entry.title: Why LLMs Fail: Tracing Reasoning Failures Inside the Model
entry.summary: Uncovering Why LLMs Fail: From Internal Mechanisms to Adversarial Reasoning Trajectories arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces CauTrace, a white-box diagnostic framework that examines how large language models fail during reasoning, using seven functional states, representation propagation, temporal-state coordination, and reasoning trajectory topology. It is evaluated on clean reasoning failures and paired adversarial perturbations across Qwen and LLaMA-family models. The failed traces show weaker Attention-MLP agreement on support-state updates and less verification relative to commitment, with exact signatures varying by architecture.

entry.title: TRIDENT-Seq: Label-Efficient Payment Risk Modeling via Profile-Matched Prefix-Future Contrast
entry.summary: TRIDENT-Seq: Profile-Matched Prefix-Future Contrast for Label-Efficient Payment Risk Modeling arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents TRIDENT-Seq, a transaction foundation model pretrained on unlabeled payment histories using Prefix-Future Contrast (PFC), which matches each prefix to summaries of subsequent behavior among candidates with similar activity profiles. Across three production payment businesses, the pretrained encoder improves average precision and recall at a 0.5% intervention budget over scratch training with the same architecture. In a deployment evaluation at Ant International, recorded amount-based chargeback and overall loss rates are 37.7% and 37.9% lower than those of the previous XGBoost-based system. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes profile-matched prefix-future contrast; the authors report recall rising from 5.64% (random candidates) to 24.62%, and deployment losses 37.7% and 37.9% lower than the prior XGBoost system ac

entry.title: EmbeddingGemma 2: A Unified, Efficient Model for Multimodal Embeddings
entry.summary: EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper introduces EmbeddingGemma 2, an open model that maps text, images, audio, video, and their combinations into one shared embedding space. It uses simplified per-layer embeddings and a multi-stage training curriculum that gradually adds modalities and objectives. The authors report that it outperforms specialist models and models two to twelve times larger across embedding benchmarks, and it supports flexible deployment options for resource-constrained settings.

entry.title: Online interval selection with binary predictions: optimal consistency and robustness tradeoff
entry.summary: Online Interval Selection with Binary Predictions: Optimal Consistency and a Continuous Robustness Tradeoff arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies online interval selection where each request comes with a binary prediction of whether it belongs to a final optimal solution. Requests arrive in arbitrary order, and accepted requests may be revoked, but rejected or revoked requests cannot be recovered. The authors show that the best consistency under finite strict robustness is (3+√5)/2, and give a deterministic algorithm achieving this consistency with exact robustness φ^5. They also present a continuous family of algorithms with a tunable replacement cost, and show that randomization allows expected consistency approaching one with finite expected robustness.

entry.title: TimeLineXR: Interactively Exploring How Vision-Language Models Encode Time
entry.summary: TimeLineXR: An Interactive Exploration of Time in Vision-Language Models arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents TimeLineXR, an interactive demo that turns the time axis inside vision-language models into a 3D scene. Users can upload images on a web page or in a WebXR environment and see each placed on a color-coded time axis. The system lets users compare where objects land and read their estimated first year of appearance.

entry.title: Aligning institutional power with operational ability
entry.summary: Aligning Institutional Power and Operational Ability arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper examines how multi-agent AI systems should be designed so that responsibilities match the abilities needed to fulfil them. It proposes a formal framework based on process-oriented modelling and institutional power to analyse normatively relevant processes. The authors also discuss strategies for repairing such processes and explain how the relation between operational processes and institutional states affects the lifecycle of normative positions.

entry.title: CodeCap-Bench: Can code serve as a good video caption? A benchmark testing whether executable code can describe video content.
entry.summary: CodeCap-Bench: Can Code Serve as a Good Video Caption? arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper explores describing videos with executable code, using graphical primitives, layout rules, and time functions instead of natural language. In question answering and video reconstruction tasks, code captions outperform natural language captions. The authors introduce CodeCap-Bench, which contains 323 videos, to test multimodal large language models on generating code captions. Leading proprietary models show promising results but still struggle with complex temporal dynamics, while open-source models lag far behind.

entry.title: EEG-based depression detection using healthy normative deviation modeling
entry.summary: Normative Deviation Modeling for EEG-based Depression Detection arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper trains structural and distributional reference models on healthy control EEG recordings to capture how an individual's EEG departs from healthy patterns. It proposes two diagnostic approaches: one summarizes deviations into scalar scores, and the other keeps dimension-wise residuals and fuses them with attention-based aggregation. Experiments on two public EEG datasets, under subject-independent within-source and cross-source settings, show the approach is effective.

entry.title: CoS-VQ: Coordinated Shared-Scale Vector Quantization for Large Language Models
entry.summary: CoS-VQ: Coordinated Shared-Scale Vector Quantization for Large Language Models arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes CoS-VQ, a vector quantization method for low-bit weight compression of large language models. It keeps codewords low-dimensional while jointly optimizing each position's index and a shared scale, addressing the coupling between scale and codeword combinations. On Qwen3.8-27B, the authors report it outperforms QTIP and LLVQ on the evaluated language modeling, coding, and reasoning benchmarks.

entry.title: WCC: A Learning Framework for Deciding When to Use Cooperative Coevolution in Large-Scale Optimization
entry.summary: WCC: A Learning-Based Framework for Deciding When to Apply Cooperative Coevolution in Large-Scale Optimization arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes WCC, a learning-based framework that decides when to apply Cooperative Coevolution (CC) in large-scale global optimization. It formulates the decision as a Markov decision process and uses an auto-regressive policy to switch dynamically between CC and non-decomposition algorithms while allocating the computational budget. The authors report strong competitiveness and generalization across problems, optimization horizons, and baseline optimizers.

entry.title: ScIntBench: Testing whether generated 3D rooms hold up when objects are physically manipulated
entry.summary: ScIntBench: Physical Interaction Plausibility in 3D Scene Generation arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper introduces ScIntBench, a benchmark for text-conditioned 3D indoor scene generation that focuses on interaction readiness. It runs prescribed actions such as pushing, opening, and surface probing in a physics simulator and measures task success, post-interaction integrity, and dynamic plausibility. The authors evaluate 12 state-of-the-art scene generation systems across 10 room types and find that strong static physical performance does not guarantee interaction readiness, with the best system succeeding on only 36.92% of tasks.

entry.title: Loss function that keeps fine-scale weather details in kilometre-scale AI forecasts
entry.summary: Scale-aware and spatially-localised optimisation of kilometre-scale MLWP models arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper introduces a wavelet-based loss function that constrains atmospheric fields by scale, location, and orientation to preserve fine-scale structure in kilometre-scale machine-learning weather prediction. It is evaluated in a joint global-regional configuration producing 1.5 km forecasts over the UK alongside roughly 31 km global forecasts. Compared with mean-squared error and an FFT-based spectral objective, the wavelet loss substantially improves spectral fidelity while keeping pointwise accuracy similar to MSE training and improving neighbourhood-based verification.

entry.title: UCVE: Graph-Structured Retrieval for Checking Compliance Requirements
entry.summary: UCVE: Graph Structured Retrieval for Compliance Validation arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper introduces UCVE, a framework for checking whether a document satisfies, violates, or fails to address every obligation in a predefined set of compliance requirements. It represents the requirements as a graph and uses reinforcement-learning-weighted spectral reranking for retrieval. Across three compliance domains, UCVE averages a 4.3% matched-K recall gain over flat cosine retrieval and outperforms strong baselines.

entry.title: Hierarchical sparse graph for linking event-camera tracklets across multiple batches
entry.summary: Hierarchical Sparse Graph for Multi-dimensional Assignment in Event-based Tracking arXiv · Oct 27, 2026Existing event-based trackers link tracklets only between adjacent batches, which fails under long occlusions or missed detections. This paper performs multi-dimensional assignment that associates tracklets across several batches at once, using fuzzy logic to quantify pairwise correlations and a Hierarchical Sparse Graph to model them. The assignment is solved as a graph partition task with a training-free heuristic. On the eTram and Ev-UAV event datasets, the method outperforms existing event-based methods and most image-based association models, reaching over twice OC-SORT's performance in many-to-many association.

entry.title: AnalogScout: PVT-Aware Analog Circuit Sizing with LLM Agents for Simulation Efficiency
entry.summary: AnalogScout: Simulation-Efficient PVT-Aware Analog Sizing with LLM Agents arXiv · Oct 27, 2026AnalogScout is a framework for sizing analog devices so that they meet specifications across all process, voltage, and temperature corners. It reuses verified elite designs and applies analytic gm/Id local sizing before global refinement, reducing the number of costly simulations. On three SKY130 OTAs with a budget of 16k simulations, it cuts power by 43.3% relative to CMA-ES and reaches CMA-ES's final power after 7.0% of that budget.

entry.title: ReForest: Combining Interpretability and Reasoning in Isolation Forest for Anomaly Detection
entry.summary: ReForest: Interpretability Meets Reasoning in Isolation Forest arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes ReForest, a framework that combines the statistical efficiency of Isolation Forest with the semantic reasoning of large language models for anomaly detection. It converts Isolation Forest's decision paths into natural-language explanations and uses an uncertainty-aware dynamic ensemble to weigh statistical and semantic signals. Experiments on four real-world healthcare and finance datasets report an average 21% improvement in Recall and a 10% gain in F1-score.

entry.title: A lightweight attention CNN with saliency maps for explainable skin cancer detection
entry.summary: A Lightweight Attention-Based CNN with Saliency-Map Interpretability for Skin Cancer Detection arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes a lightweight attention-based convolutional neural network (CNN-Attention) for binary classification of skin lesions, incorporating saliency maps to visualize regions that influence its decisions. Channel attention is used to focus on informative areas of dermoscopic images while keeping computational cost low. On a public dataset of 2,637 training and 660 test images, the model achieved 87 percent accuracy with 1.95 million parameters and 7.45 MB storage, matching MobileNet while using about half the parameters and storage. Its ROC AUC and PR AUC were 0.9475 and 0.9430.

entry.title: MvT: Event-camera multi-object tracking using multi-view projection
entry.summary: MvT: Event-based Multi-view Projection for Multiple Object Tracking arXiv · Oct 27, 2026Event cameras output asynchronous data, and common methods convert it into pseudo-frames, which can cause tracking failures when trajectories overlap or are close. This paper proposes MvT, a multi-view tracking pipeline that keeps a 2D format while adding spatio-temporal views to resolve single-view ambiguities, then fuses results in a 3D coordinate system and associates tracklets via an optimization model. The method is training-free and was evaluated on four datasets, including the authors' Small Objects Dataset (SOD), where it outperforms existing trackers.

entry.title: Probing structured internal representations to anticipate risks in end-to-end self-driving
entry.summary: Structured Representation Probing for Risk Anticipation in End-to-End Autonomous Driving arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper introduces the Structured Representation Probe (SRP), a lightweight monitor that reads actor, ego, and map representations from a frozen driving policy to anticipate failures. It learns a separate linear risk direction for each source and uses event-window supervision to link the readout to upcoming hard failures. On Bench2Drive with DriveTransformer, the probe reaches an ROC-AUC of 0.833 at a 2-second horizon, compared with 0.715 for temporal consistency, at 2.67% readout runtime overhead.

entry.title: TRUCO: A Scalable Lock-Free Parallel Algorithm for Extracting Contours
entry.summary: TRUCO: A Scalable Lock-Free Algorithm for Parallel Contour Extraction arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents TRUCO, a lock-free parallel algorithm that converts binary masks into geometric contours. It uses a start-point ownership rule and a speculative tracing model so that each contour is processed exactly once. Experiments on synthetic and real-world data, run on consumer and server-grade CPUs, reportedly show significant speedups over existing baselines, over an order of magnitude compared with the industry standard, with good scalability on high-resolution scenes.

entry.title: Multi-Label Agreement: A Framework for Measuring Annotator Consistency
entry.summary: Multi-Label Agreement: A Flexible Framework for Inter-Annotator Reliability arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper introduces Multi-Label Agreement (MLA), a flexible framework for measuring how consistently annotators label items in multi-label tasks. It keeps each item's full binary label vector and uses average pairwise Hamming agreement, counting both joint selections and joint omissions. Through a worked example and Monte Carlo simulations, the paper shows how results depend on label prevalence, the declared label inventory, and the chosen expected-agreement model. A Python implementation is also provided.

entry.title: Improving noise initialization for zero-shot video restoration using image diffusion models
entry.summary: Taming Noise Initialization for Zero-shot Video Restoration with Image Diffusion Priors arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes a zero-shot video restoration method that uses a pre-trained image diffusion model instead of a costly video diffusion model. It generates initial noise by applying DDIM inversion to the corrupted video frames, preserving temporal correlations between frames. The authors add an adaptive noise blending strategy and measurement-guided trajectory attention to improve temporal consistency. The method is reported to outperform existing zero-shot approaches on the DAVIS, REDS4, and Set8 datasets.

entry.title: Bayesian Inference for Expensive Simulators: A Survey and Comparison of Design Choices
entry.summary: Bayesian Inference of Expensive Simulators: Survey and Comparison of Design Choices arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper surveys Bayesian inference methods that use simulators as forward models, especially when simulations are very costly. It unifies existing Bayesian optimization-based approaches into one framework and systematically compares design choices by the simulation budget they require. The authors find the surrogate model's response variable strongly affects efficiency and propose custom proxy variables, with a Julia package provided.

entry.title: RPSD: Retrieval-privileged on-policy self-distillation with optimal transport for recommendation
entry.summary: RPSD: Retrieval-Privileged On-Policy Self-Distillation with Optimal Transport arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper addresses sequential recommendation with LLMs, where reinforcement learning shares one sequence-level reward across all tokens and relies on a single user's data. The proposed RPSD method uses on-policy self-distillation, in which a teacher with privileged knowledge re-evaluates the student's responses to assign token-specific credit. It also uses temporally aware optimal transport and diversity-aware selection to draw complementary behavioral evidence from similar users. The authors report state-of-the-art performance across multiple real-world datasets.

entry.title: Using directed acyclic graphs to model how user preferences depend on each other in narrative-driven recommendation
entry.summary: Modeling Preference Dependencies with Directed Acyclic Graphs for Narrative-Driven Recommendation arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes the Preference Dependency Graph Framework (PDG-F) for recommendations based on free-form user narratives in which preferences qualify one another. The system parses a request into a directed acyclic Preference Dependency Graph, retrieves candidate evidence from the open Web along its paths, and ranks results by topological path ranking. Experiments across three domains in English and Chinese show it outperforms baselines, open-domain retrieval agents, and frontier language models.

entry.title: Where to Spend the Evaluation Budget in LLM-Driven Agent Scaffold Evolution
entry.summary: Where Should the Evaluation Budget Go in LLM-Driven Agent Scaffold Evolution? arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies how to allocate limited evaluation budgets when LLM-driven systems evolve agent workflows through repeated candidate generation and testing. The authors find that sparse feedback can sustain productive evolution, while extra targeted evaluation improves the final choice of scaffold. They propose \method, which combines sparse search-time feedback with targeted final confirmation and reuses accumulated observations. Across four benchmarks and two evolution frameworks, it achieves higher mean performance than full evaluation in most settings while using about half as many evaluation cells.

entry.title: Low-degree polynomial lower bounds for clustering in low dimensions
entry.summary: Low-degree polynomials lower bounds for clustering in small dimension arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper studies the computational limits of clustering n observations from a mixture of K isotropic distributions in R^d when K is much larger than d. It constructs a mixture of Bernoulli product distributions whose centers come from a dual BCH code, so that moment tensors match those of the uniform distribution up to a given order. For suitable separations, low-degree polynomials require roughly K^2 d^{3/2} observations, and via Gaussianization the hardness extends to isotropic Gaussian mixtures. ★★★★ Notable: The authors build a mixture of 2K product Bernoulli distributions from dual BCH codes so that moment tensors match the uniform distribution up to order 2m+1. entry.title: GradCO: A Behavior-Aware Method for Text-Based Person Anomaly Search That Reduces Gradient Conflicts
entry.summary: GradCO: Behavior-Aware Gradient-Conflict Offloading for Text-Based Person Anomaly Search arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper introduces GradCO, a method for Text-based Person Anomaly Search, which finds a target pedestrian using descriptions of appearance and normal or anomalous behavior. It combines three components: Behavior-Aware Mixture-of-Experts, Conflict Offload Learning to reduce conflicting gradients, and Hierarchical Intent Alignment that aggregates expert similarities with query-conditioned weights. The authors report that GradCO significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods on five TPAS/TIPR benchmarks.

entry.title: REGLAT at ArGuard: An Ensemble Model Adding Entity Recognition to Detect Harmful Arabic Content
entry.summary: REGLAT at ArGuard Shared Tasks: An Ensemble-Based Model Integrating NER for Harmful Content Detection in Arabic arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes a two-stage method that classifies Arabic user prompts into seven harmful-content categories. GLiNER first extracts harm-related entities, which are appended to the original text and passed to a fine-tuned MARBERT classifier. On the ArGuard 2026 development set it reached a macro-F1 of 0.886 and accuracy of 0.897. On the blind test set it scored 0.793 accuracy and 0.735 macro-F1 for subtask 1, and 0.770 accuracy and 0.754 macro-F1 for subtask 2. The authors note that distinguishing related categories remains difficult.

entry.title: GameVerse: A Minute-Scale Gameplay Video Dataset for Long-Horizon Interactive World Modeling
entry.summary: GameVerse: A Minute-Scale Gameplay Dataset for Long-Horizon Interactive World Modeling arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper introduces GameVerse, a gameplay video dataset built for training interactive world models over minute-long horizons. It contains 69.7K clips totaling 1,655 hours and 349.6 million frames, including 1,358 hours of continuous two-minute sequences. Each clip has a camera trajectory that stays coherent across minutes and captions aligned to event boundaries. The authors report that training on GameVerse substantially extends the temporal horizon of interactive world models.

entry.title: Your Policy Is Secretly a Harness: How Agent Interfaces Shape Decisions
entry.summary: Your Policy Is Secretly a Harness: The Decision Geometry of Agent Interfaces arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper studies how language model agents depend on their harness, the prompts, tools, and control logic that present tasks to the model. Under KL-regularized control, the authors show that a trained policy's log odds reflect its harness's action preferences, and that deployed return equals the harness ceiling minus the policy's mismatch. In MiniWoB++, reversing observation field order drops a trained model's success from 85.0% to 19.2%. ★★★★ Notable: Under KL-regularized control, optimal-policy log odds reflect harness action preferences, and deployed return splits into harness ceiling minus policy mismatch. entry.title: Safety alignment of large language models in Hausa, an African language
entry.summary: Aligning Large Language Models for Safety in African Languages: A Case Study of Hausa arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper examines how well large language models are aligned for safety in Hausa, a low-resource language spoken in West Africa. The authors build HausaSafeLM, a Hausa safety preference dataset of 10,000 prompts with human-corrected and machine-translated examples, and compare supervised fine-tuning with direct preference optimization. They find that refusal-rate metrics alone can misleadingly suggest a base model is safe, and that no configuration jointly maximizes safety, helpfulness, and fluency.

entry.title: TCM-DiagCommit: A Benchmark for Evidence-Based Traditional Chinese Medicine Syndrome Selection and Decision Commitment
entry.summary: TCM-DiagCommit: A TCM-SD-Derived Benchmark for Evidence-Conditioned Syndrome Selection and Commitment arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper introduces TCM-DiagCommit, a benchmark built from the public TCM-SD/ZY-BERT resource, converting 1,834 cases into 23,842 task rows over 148 syndrome labels. It uses candidate sets of varying difficulty and staged evidence, plus tongue/pulse perturbations and insufficient-evidence variants. The authors argue that final-answer accuracy alone is insufficient, and that answer selection, evidence use, and commitment should be measured separately.

entry.title: GraphRAGProv: Combining GraphRAG with How-Provenance Tracking
entry.summary: GraphRAGProv: GraphRAG Meets How-Provenance arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper presents GraphRAGProv, an architecture that runs SPARQL queries over RDF knowledge graphs linked to their source text to compute answers and how-provenance polynomials. These polynomials record which statement occurrences were used and how they were combined. Each statement links back to its source, so users can check whether extracted statements reflect the text and whether the query combines them correctly. An interactive demo examines 400 cases from two multi-hop QA benchmarks and finds extraction and query errors even when the final answer is correct.

entry.title: HDVS: Semi-Supervised Segmentation with Heterogeneous Dual-Branch Voting
entry.summary: HDVS: semi-supervised semantic segmentation via heterogeneous dual-branch voting supervision arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes HDVS, a semi-supervised semantic segmentation framework that learns from many unlabeled images with fewer human annotations. Built on cross-supervision, it adds a voting mechanism that combines pseudo-labels from heterogeneous branches to improve their reliability. A feature communication module introduces feature-level perturbations to increase prediction diversity between the two branches. The method is evaluated on PASCAL VOC 2012 and Cityscapes and is reported to outperform state-of-the-art approaches.

entry.title: Doubly Robust Deep Kernel Tests: checks whether two interventions produce the same outcome distribution for high-dimensional structured data like images, text, and graphs.
entry.summary: Doubly Robust Deep Kernel Tests for Structured Outcomes arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes DR-KTE-Deep, a test of whether two interventions induce the same outcome distribution when outcomes are structured and high-dimensional, such as images, text, and graphs. It represents interventional distributions as mean embeddings on learned deep features, with the treatment effect expressed as a doubly robust representation, and optimises the features to maximise estimated test power. Empirically, the method achieves substantially higher power than fixed and bandwidth-optimised kernel baselines across image, text and graph outcomes while keeping Type-I error well calibrated.

entry.title: Subspace Clifford Networks: a neural network design that replaces global cyclic shifts with grouped subspace interactions
entry.summary: Subspace Clifford Networks arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes Subspace Clifford Networks, which replace sampling sparse cyclic diagonals across the whole channel space with interactions inside small grouped subspaces. Features are projected into groups of two to four dimensions, with wedge coordinates and coordinate-wise products computed within each group and cross-group mixing done by learnable 1×1 projections. Experiments on CIFAR-100 report substantially fewer parameters and shorter training time, and the hierarchical variants achieve higher accuracy than the evaluated shift-based hierarchical baselines.

entry.title: Sharpness-Aware Muon: a Muon optimizer variant that seeks flatter minima
entry.summary: Sharpness-Aware Muon: Matrix-Aware Optimization with Momentum-Guided Perturbations arXiv · Oct 27, 2026Muon is a matrix-aware optimizer that uses momentum and orthogonalization but does not explicitly control worst-case loss in a neighborhood. The paper introduces MuSAM, which adds SAM-style perturbations to Muon's orthogonalized update, and MoMuSAM, which uses normalized momentum as the perturbation direction to avoid an extra gradient evaluation. The authors prove both methods reach the same asymptotic first-order stationarity order, with MoMuSAM giving a more stable stochastic linearization. Experiments on standard benchmarks show sharpness awareness consistently improves Muon.

entry.title: Spine: A method that organizes long coding-agent work into subtask trees for shorter, structured context
entry.summary: Spine: Compiling Subtask Trees into Structured Context for Long-Horizon Coding Agents arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents Spine, an interface and runtime that lets coding agents declare explicit subtask boundaries and records them in a persistent tree. Before each model call, unfinished subtasks keep their interactions while completed ones are replaced by their results. The authors integrate Spine into Codex and Pi and report score and cost changes on benchmarks such as SWE-Milestone and ProgramBench compared with the native versions.

entry.title: Vision-Language-Action or World-Action? Just Action Models
entry.summary: Vision-Language-Action or World-Action? Just Action Models arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper examines whether robot control policies should inherit knowledge from vision-language models or visual generators. The authors separate three choices: backbone initialization, the objective for future observations, and whether future-prediction machinery is kept at inference. They propose the Just Action Model (JAM), a pretrained visual backbone with an action expert trained using an action loss and a foresight loss, where the foresight prediction head is discarded after training. JAM outperforms matched FastWAM and ImageWAM policies on LIBERO and LIBERO-Plus and performs similarly or slightly better on RoboTwin, and with cached foresight targets it reduces estimated training FLOPs per sample by 73% relative to FastWAM.

entry.title: TopoField: Technical Report for the ECCV 2026 SceneFun3D Challenge
entry.summary: TopoField: Technical Report for ECCV 2026 SceneFun3D Challenge arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This report addresses functional segmentation, which locates small interactive parts such as knobs, buttons, and sockets in indoor point clouds and outputs confidence-ranked instance masks. TopoField, a deterministic decoder built on VOLT, fuses 13 test-time forward passes into a semantic consensus field, decodes instance candidates from its geometry, and ranks them class-aware. It achieves 28.286% AP, 41.383% AP50, and 47.558% AP25 on 561 validation instances across 30 scenes, and placed second in the ECCV 2026 SceneFun3D Challenge.

entry.title: Zhengrong-Spatial-Aware 1.0: Advancing 3D Multimodal AI for Spatial Reasoning
entry.summary: Zhengrong-Spatial-Aware 1.0: Advancing 3D Multimodal Intelligence arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This report presents two end-to-end pipelines for adapting multimodal models to answer questions about 3D spatial scenes. One fine-tunes HiSpatial-3B, which adds metric-scale 3D point maps to RGB images, while the other applies QLoRA fine-tuning to Qwen3-VL. On the target spatial benchmark, HiSpatial's overall accuracy rose from 1.73% to 79.89%, and Qwen3-VL-8B and 32B improved from 20.74% to 45.27% and from 30.79% to 47.60%, respectively.

entry.title: Retrieve to Act: Motion Primitive Graph Retrieval for Stable Vision-Language-Action Execution
entry.summary: Retrieve to Act: Motion Primitive Graph Retrieval for Robust VLA Execution arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes R2A, a test-time framework that treats robustness of vision-language-action policies to out-of-distribution visual shifts as a geometric motion primitive retrieval problem. Successful training demonstrations are organized into an offline spatiotemporal motion primitive graph, and a graph neural network retrieves structurally compatible future primitives during execution. A learned gating mechanism combines these retrieved priors with the frozen policy's actions, and experiments on three VLA architectures report higher success rates in simulation and real-world tests.

entry.title: Retrospective macromolecular pool fraction mapping from routine clinical MRI using physics-guided self-supervised learning
entry.summary: Retrospective macromolecular pool fraction mapping from conventional clinical MRI: a physics-guided self-supervised deep learning framework arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents a deep learning framework that estimates macromolecular pool fraction (MPF), a biomarker sensitive to myelin, directly from conventional clinical brain MRI sequences (T1-weighted, T2-weighted, and FLAIR) without paired quantitative reference scans. The method embeds a two-pool magnetization transfer signal model and uses adaptive instance normalization to handle heterogeneous clinical protocols. Trained on 7,705 3 T sessions, it reported mean MPF of 0.182 in white matter and 0.144 in gray matter, with lower MPF in demyelinating lesions than in normal-appearing white matter.

entry.title: Shortcut amplification in video RLVR: a perceptual uncertainty view
entry.summary: Uncovering Shortcut Amplification in Video RLVR through the Lens of Perceptual Uncertainty Collapse arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) for improving video reasoning in large multimodal models. The authors find that outcome-level optimization makes models increasingly favor text-prior answers even when visual evidence does not support them. They propose Bifocal Self-distillation Policy Optimization (BSPO), which uses reasoning-sensitive tokens and shortcut-aware visual perturbations to regulate policy updates. Experiments reportedly show improved video reasoning performance and stronger visual faithfulness.

entry.title: SimplexLoRA: Adjusting LoRA adapter ranks during fine-tuning via simplex-based importance weights
entry.summary: SimplexLoRA: Dynamic Rank Updating via Alternating Minimization with Simplex Projection arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes SimplexLoRA, a variant of Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) that adjusts the rank of each adapter during fine-tuning based on learned importance. After a short warm-up, per-adapter importance weights optimized on an n-scaled simplex are frozen, allocating capacity without increasing the overall parameter budget or inference cost. Evaluated on 12 language understanding, summarization, and reasoning tasks with DeBERTaV3, BART-large, Llama 3.1 8B, and Qwen3-8B, it matches or outperforms standard LoRA and recent adaptive baselines, with the largest gains at low ranks.

entry.title: 3D-SceneQ: Improving 3D Language Models with Query-Guided Pruning and 2D Feature Fusion
entry.summary: 3D-SceneQ: Empowering 3D LLM With Query-Guided Adaptive Pruning and Multi-Modal Feature Enhancement arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents 3D-SceneQ, a 3D large language model for understanding 3D scenes. Its Query-Guided Adaptive Pruning module selects objects relevant to the user's instruction to reduce irrelevant noise, while its Multi-modal Object-level Feature Enhancement module adds features from pre-trained 2D models to the 3D representation. The authors report that the method outperforms current state-of-the-art approaches on several benchmarks, including +5.7 CIDEr on Scan2Cap and +17.0 EM@1 on SQA3D.

entry.title: Do Generalist Skill Optimizers Really Help AI Agents? A Bipartite Attribution Rethink
entry.summary: Does Your Generalist Skill Optimizer Really Incentivize Agentic Tasks? Rethinking Skill Optimization via Bipartite Attribution arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper introduces BiPA, a method for evaluating skill optimizers that rewrite an AI agent's natural-language procedures to improve performance on long-horizon tasks. Across three optimizers, three benchmarks, and two models, learned skills succeed about as often as their hand-written seeds, and development-set gains vanish on the test set. The optimized skills also increase input tokens by about 16%, largely because the added rules cause extra conversation turns. The authors propose four principles, including accepting only edits whose gains exceed what selection alone would report. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes BiPA, using a selection baseline and bipartite attribution: learned skills match their seed's success, dev gains vanish on test, and input tokens rise about 16%.

entry.title: How much can choosing the best of N candidate actions improve a world action model, and how to realize it in closed loop
entry.summary: How Much Can Best-of-N Help a World Action Model? Measuring Selectable Headroom and Realizing It in Closed Loop arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper studies how much a world action model can gain at test time by imagining several candidate action sequences and executing the best one. It introduces a denoised counterfactual protocol that measures the selectable headroom a selector can actually realize, and uses these measurements to build a selector that deviates from the policy only when the model predicts failure. On held-out episodes of training tasks, closed-loop success rises from 76.9% to 81.6%, and on unseen tasks from 62.6% to 69.8%.

entry.title: Action-value calibration through shared continuations for long-horizon agent RL
entry.summary: Action-Value Calibration via Continuation Sharing for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper addresses the difficulty of assigning credit to individual actions in reinforcement learning for long-horizon agents. It proposes ConCal (Continuation Calibration), which matches visits from the same task with identical state-action-state transitions, combines shared continuation evidence, and propagates calibrated values backward to refine earlier action-value estimates without extra rollouts. With Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, ConCal improves success rates over GiGPO by 3.39 points on ALFWorld and 5.86 points on WebShop.

entry.title: VGIQA: Fine-grained image quality scoring that pinpoints local flaws using visual grounding rewards
entry.summary: VGIQA: Fine-Grained Image Quality Assessment with Visual Grounding Rewards arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents VGIQA, an image quality assessment model that evaluates both overall image quality and localized quality within an image. It is trained in two stages, a cold-start phase followed by reinforcement learning, guided by reward functions designed for local quality assessment. The authors also introduce VGSR-2K, a new dataset for local quality evaluation, on which VGIQA outperforms open-source models such as Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Instruct and Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct.

entry.title: INTR++: A More Accurate, Interpretable, and Adaptable Interpretable Transformer
entry.summary: INTR++: INterpretable TRansformer with better Accuracy, Interpretability, and Adaptability arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes INTR++, which extends Prompt-CAM with a lightweight Prompt Adapter Module (PAM) that enriches prompts with domain-specific knowledge. The authors aim to keep interpretability consistent across domains with differing image characteristics, such as medical, microscopic, and remote sensing imagery. INTR++ adds only a small number of parameters compared with Prompt-CAM. The paper reports consistent improvements across animal, plant, medical, microscopic, remote sensing, and object-centric datasets.

entry.title: MLE-World: Predicting Machine Learning Experiment Results with a Learned World Model
entry.summary: MLE-World: Predicting Machine Learning Experiment Outcomes with a Learned World Model arXiv · Oct 27, 2026AI research agents normally must run each candidate program to train and evaluate models, which limits how many options they can explore. This paper introduces MLE-World, a model fine-tuned from Qwen3.5-4B that predicts a program's terminal output, including error traces, training logs, and validation scores, from its code and data description without executing it, along with a confidence score. Five test-time scaling policies guided by these predictions are built, and candidates are actually run only when confidence is low.
