On 17 MLE-bench Lite tasks, MLE-World matches real terminal output on 77.9% of held-out programs, compared with 41.1% for much larger prompted models.

entry.title: Rényi-Regularized Flow Variational Inference for Bayesian Calibration
entry.summary: Rènyi-Regularized Flow-Based Variational Inference for Bayesian Calibration arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies normalizing-flow variational inference for Bayesian model calibration, where posteriors with several modes separated by low-probability regions can cause mode collapse. Using a two-parameter twin experiment, the authors add a regularization term based on Rényi divergence that encourages the approximate posterior to cover the prior support. The near-collapse fraction drops from 50% to 25% in this experiment. The authors note that the regularization alters the Bayesian variational objective, introduces a trade-off in approximation accuracy, and is not a general solution to mode collapse.

entry.title: LiveSearch: A Live Benchmark for Financial Search Agents Using Executable Verifier Code
entry.summary: LiveSearch: Questions as Executable Verifier Code for a Live Benchmark of Professional-Source Financial Search Agents arXiv · Oct 27, 2026LiveSearch is a live benchmark for financial search agents that stores each question as executable code calling a professional financial data service. The gold answer is recomputed at evaluation time and re-executed daily without human or language model involvement, so memorized answers become outdated. Six tool-calling models reached 70.9% to 76.7% accuracy under general web search. Over three consecutive days, 70% of questions changed their gold value.

entry.title: Benchmark testing whether retrievers handle evidence that contradicts their prior knowledge
entry.summary: Coverage Under Contradiction: A Benchmark for Negation-Aware Retrieval arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper introduces CoverageBench-Negate, a benchmark that tests whether retrieval systems find corpus evidence when it contradicts their parametric knowledge. The authors create negated versions of each nugget and edit supporting documents to match the negation while preserving context, yielding about 63,000 original-edited evidence pairs across six datasets. In baseline experiments, BM25 distinguishes original from edited evidence much better than dense retrievers such as Qwen3 and Jina, which perform near chance.

entry.title: WorkFactory: Converting Professional Intents into Executable Tasks to Scale Agent Training
entry.summary: WorkFactory: Turning Professional Intents into Executable Work for Scalable Agent Training arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper presents WorkFactory, a framework that builds an information support graph from professional intents and uses probe executions to find and repair missing task information. It constructs 112,686 tasks across 612 occupations and fine-tunes Qwen models on the resulting teacher trajectories, producing the WorkPilot family. The authors report that all three models improve over their base models on four professional-work benchmarks. ★★★★ Notable: WorkFactory plans with an information support graph and repairs via probe executions to build 612-occupation professional tasks (112,686 total); the authors report WorkPilot-35B-A3B rising from 879 to

entry.title: Physics-Guided Flow Matching: A Generative AI Model for Forecasting Global Electron Content
entry.summary: Physics-Guided Flow Matching: A Generative AI Framework for Global Total Electron Content Forecasting arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes a physics-guided generative AI framework for day-ahead forecasting of global total electron content (TEC), which matters for space weather monitoring and satellite communication and navigation. The model builds on flow matching and incorporates ionospheric dynamics described by a partial differential equation into the transformation process, combining them with statistical patterns learned from data and adaptively weighting each location. Trained and evaluated on one year of global TEC data from the TIEGCM model, it outperforms representative benchmarks at all lead times and across latitudes.

entry.title: What survives when GPT-2 is distilled into a smaller model: a mechanistic interpretability study.
entry.summary: What Survives Distillation? A Mechanistic Interpretability Study of GPT-2 and DistilGPT-2 arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper compares GPT-2 with its six-layer distilled student, DistilGPT-2, using CKA, logit lens, attention analysis, sparse autoencoders, and activation patching. It examines two circuits: Indirect Object Identification, which collapses after distillation, and Greater-Than, which largely survives by remapping a layer-9 head to layer 4. The authors conclude that circuit compressibility determines mechanistic survival under distillation.

entry.title: FastBEVFusion: A Simple Fast Fusion Method for 3D Object Detection at 50 FPS
entry.summary: FastBEVFusion: Simple Multi-Modal Fusion for 3D Object Detection at 50 FPS arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper proposes FastBEVFusion, a simple, fast, and robust system that fuses LiDAR and camera data for 3D object detection. It projects modality-specific features into semi-aligned BEV spaces without depending on depth estimation, and combines them with a lightweight, dynamic cross-attention fusion module. According to the paper, experiments on nuScenes show it outperforms existing real-time systems, runs at over 50 FPS without deployment libraries, and is robust to calibration errors.

entry.title: GCSR-OCC: Geometry Calibration and Semantic Routing for Open-Vocabulary Occupancy Prediction
entry.summary: GCSR-OCC: Geometry Calibration and Semantic Routing for Open-Vocabulary Occupancy Prediction arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents GCSR-OCC, a method for predicting indoor 3D occupancy from a single RGB image, recognizing objects beyond predefined categories. It calibrates Gaussian-based geometry to suppress scale inflation and excessive overlap, and uses text-conditioned semantic routing to reduce semantic mixing within Gaussians. On Occ-ScanNet, without 3D semantic annotations, it reports 63.31% geometric IoU and 27.44% semantic mIoU, and lowers geometric aggregation latency from 19.76 ms to 12.88 ms.

entry.title: Variational Optimal Control for Diffusion Guidance
entry.summary: Variational Optimal Control for Diffusion Guidance arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes a variational control framework that links sampling-time guidance and reward-based model adaptation through a shared Jacobian pullback. The proposed Variational Optimal Guidance (VOG) acts in state space through the denoising Jacobian, while Distilled Variational Optimal Control (DVOC) amortizes locally improved endpoints into model parameters. On ImageNet, the authors report that VOG lowers DiT-XL/2 FID from 2.27 to 2.04 at 250 steps and from 7.58 to 4.44 at 25 steps.

entry.title: Fisher-Shaped EWC: a replay-free continual learning method that shapes solutions for future retention
entry.summary: Beyond Parameter Protection: Fisher-Shaped EWC for Replay-Free Continual Learning arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes Fisher-Shaped EWC (FS-EWC), which extends the Fisher information matrix's role from protecting parameters to forming solutions that are less sensitive to future updates. During task learning it minimizes the worst-case empirical Fisher trace within a neighborhood, and at task completion it builds the retained solution by trajectory-based model merging. Experiments across benchmarks show improvements over EWC, with a better stability-plasticity balance and greater tolerance to parameter drift.

entry.title: Generative replay for training Hopfield networks without forgetting past tasks
entry.summary: Generative Replay for Equilibrium Propagation: Toward Edge-Friendly Continual Learning in Hopfield Networks arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper addresses catastrophic forgetting in Hopfield networks trained with Equilibrium Propagation during continual learning. It proposes Energy-Based Generative Replay (EB-Gen), where a frozen copy of the network generates pseudo-samples for rehearsal, so no external data buffer is needed. Evaluated on Split MNIST and Split CIFAR10 in the class-incremental setting, the method reports 75% and 64% average accuracy, respectively.

entry.title: MixSIS: Instance segmentation that mixes annotation types
entry.summary: MixSIS: Mixed-supervised instance segmentation arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes Mixed-Supervised Instance Segmentation (MixSIS), a task where a dataset can combine image, point, box, and mask annotations. The authors introduce AnnotationsMixer (AnnsMixer) as a baseline that generates pseudo mask annotations from all these annotation levels, even within a single image. The paper reports that AnnsMixer largely outperforms state-of-the-art methods on weakly-supervised and MixSIS tasks, and shows in three case studies how it can reduce annotation time or improve results. ★★★★ Notable: Introduces MixSIS, a new task mixing image, point, box, and mask annotations, and the AnnsMixer baseline that generates pseudo masks from mixed levels within one image. The authors report large gains

entry.title: What the Primary Lund Plane Omits: A Diagnosis of a Jet-Tagger Representation Gap
entry.summary: What the Primary Lund Plane Omits: A Model-Stitching Diagnosis of a Jet-Tagger Representation Gap arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper uses model stitching to test whether the performance gap between Lund-plane jet taggers and Particle Transformer (ParT) comes from a weaker representation or a weaker downstream computation. Using only the primary declustering branch, the representation shows lower background rejection than ParT, indicating a representational deficit. Rebuilding the representation on the full Cambridge/Aachen declustering tree closes 72% of the gap.

entry.title: Physics-guided diffusion model for exposure interpolation in HDR imaging
entry.summary: Physics Guided Diffusion Model Based Exposure Interpolation for High Dynamic Range Imaging arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper addresses brightness order reversal artifacts that arise when fusing two large-exposure-ratio standard dynamic range images captured in a single shot. It proposes a physics-guided diffusion model based exposure interpolation algorithm, where a physics-driven component produces an initial interpolated image and a diffusion model component generates residual high-frequency details. Experimental results are reported to validate the proposed algorithm.

entry.title: MRI-to-CT Spinal Image Translation Using Anatomy-Guided Pseudo-Pairing and Adversarial Diffusion
entry.summary: MRI-to-CT Translation of Spinal Images via Anatomy-Guided Pseudo-Pairing and Adversarial Diffusion arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes a three-stage framework that synthesizes CT-like images from spinal MRI to support surgical planning without extra radiation. It matches unpaired MRI and CT slices using vertebral segmentations and rigid registration to create pseudo-paired training data, then trains an adversarial diffusion model for translation. A 3D refinement network improves continuity between slices. On 83 MRI volumes, the approach raised the binary 3D vertebral Dice score from 0.666 to 0.739 compared with diffusion alone.

entry.title: MCP-Net: A Coronary Perception Network for Robotic Guidewire Guidance
entry.summary: MCP-Net: Real-Time Coronary Perception Network and Topological Analysis for Robotic Guidewire Navigation arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents a simulation-driven framework for robotic guidewire navigation centered on MCP-Net, a multi-task network. From a single two-dimensional fluoroscopic frame, it jointly performs coronary vessel segmentation, guidewire-tip localization, and stenosis localization. The predictions are converted into a structured vascular graph with centerlines, bifurcations, endpoints, and branch angles, from which a roadmap toward the target lesion is generated.

entry.title: Hidden Internal Damage from Pruning Transformer Language Models
entry.summary: Mechanistic Failure Modes of Weight Pruning in Transformer Language Models arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies how weight pruning affects GPT-2 by testing combinations of importance criteria, component types, and sparsity levels against the indirect object identification (IOI) circuit. Using activation patching and related causal methods, it identifies two distinct failure modes: magnitude pruning of attention heads destroys the circuit, leaving the model near chance, while magnitude pruning of 30% of MLP neurons keeps the circuit intact but flips the sign of Name Mover contributions, yielding 17.7% accuracy. The authors note that perplexity rates the neuron-pruned model as less damaged than random head pruning. They conclude that output metrics and structural checks can miss such mechanistic damage, and recommend circuit-level causal analysis for evaluating compressed language models.

entry.title: SFE-O: A Knowledge Ontology for Supercritical CO2 Biomass Extraction
entry.summary: SFE-O: An Ontology for Knowledge-Grounded AI in Supercritical CO₂ Biomass Extraction and Fractionation arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents SFE-O, a modular OWL 2 ontology that describes supercritical CO2 biomass extraction processes. It links biomass, process, and product dimensions and explicitly represents process topology, parameter provenance, mass-transfer phenomena, and constant and falling extraction rate mechanisms. The ontology is evaluated through a pilot-scale extraction batch example, a reasoner-based consistency check, and a competency-question SPARQL query.

entry.title: Prospector: a compact model that learns to traverse knowledge graphs for scientific reasoning
entry.summary: Prospector: learning a compact graph traversal policy for scientific reasoning arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper presents Prospector, a compact model trained to reason over a domain knowledge graph by traversing it step by step. It calls a small set of tools one at a time to build context and answers with an evidence chain that can be checked edge by edge against the retrieved graph content. Trained only on a semiconductor-manufacturing graph, it is reported to transfer to unseen graphs from three other fields.

entry.title: Multibranch ensemble head for efficient cucumber growth-stage classification with vision foundation models
entry.summary: Multibranch Ensemble Head in Vision Foundation Models for Efficient Cucumber Phenological Stage Classification arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes a regularizing multibranch ensemble head for vision foundation models such as DINOv2, which samples one branch stochastically during training and averages both branches' probabilities at inference. On the NALEF Food Safety dataset of five cucumber growth stages, the DINOv2 ViT-S model with this head reaches a Macro F1 of 0.978 and Cohen's Kappa of 0.971. It requires 12.2 GFlops and 22.3M parameters, which the authors state makes it deployable on smartphones and edge devices.

entry.title: Self-Regularized Flow Language Models: a method that uses the denoising trajectory to improve continuous diffusion language model training
entry.summary: Self-Regularized Flow Language Models arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper introduces SERF, a self-supervised framework that improves continuous diffusion language models through noisy-to-clean self-distillation. An EMA teacher receives a cleaner version of the student's noisy input along the same interpolation path and provides additional supervision. Two variants, SERF-L and SERF-P, are tested across three continuous language-model paradigms, showing gains in training efficiency, generation quality, and few-step generation.

entry.title: Restoring Diversity in Distilled Diffusion Models via a First-Step Bias
entry.summary: A First-Step Bias Restores Lost Diversity in Diffusion Model Distillation arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper addresses the loss of output diversity in diffusion models distilled to generate images in a few steps. The authors find that most of this diversity loss occurs in the first, high-noise denoising step. They propose ReSeed, which adds a seed-response bias adapter only to the first student step, aligning its velocity with the teacher's, while all other weights and steps stay frozen. Experiments on several text-to-image and text-to-video models show improved diversity with competitive visual quality and very few additional trainable parameters.

entry.title: Generating Text in Low-Resource Languages with Human-Curated Vocabularies
entry.summary: Text Generation in Low-Resource Languages Using Human-Curated Vocabularies arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper examines whether large language models can generate coherent text in extremely low-resource and unseen languages by using human-curated vocabularies. The framework combines these vocabularies with a small number of human-written exemplars that supply syntactic signals, sampling candidate words from a Zipfian distribution. Generated text is evaluated for lexical diversity, off-target ratio, and human fluency judgments. Reasoning-enabled models produced fluent sentence-level text and showed promising paragraph-level performance.

entry.title: Hardware-matched spiking networks for real-time Purkinje cell spike sorting
entry.summary: Hardware-Matched Spiking Neural Networks for Real-Time Purkinje Cell Spike Classification arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents two compact spiking neural networks that separate Purkinje cell simple spikes from complex spikes on untethered recording headstages. ConvSNN targets a microcontroller's matrix vector processor, while StreamSNN targets a dedicated SKY130 circuit. On cells unseen during training, complex-spike F1 scores are 0.873 for ConvSNN and 0.837 for StreamSNN, both with eight-bit weights.

entry.title: SplatScout: Query-driven part-level referring segmentation in 3D Gaussian scenes
entry.summary: SplatScout: Query-Driven Part-Level Referring Segmentation in Gaussian Scenes arXiv · Oct 27, 2026Existing referring segmentation methods for Gaussian scenes mainly target whole objects, choosing among fixed candidates produced by a segmenter. SplatScout is a closed-loop approach in which a vision-language model actively selects views, directs segmentation, and inspects rendered 3D results to refine its predictions. The authors introduce PartRef-ScanNet++, a part-level benchmark with 261 manually verified queries across 12 ScanNet++ scenes, where SplatScout reaches 0.538 mIoU. It also scores higher than existing methods on four other referring benchmarks.

entry.title: TriDifNet: A Unified Diffusion Network for Joint Infrared-Visible Alignment, Fusion, and Pedestrian Detection
entry.summary: TriDifNet: A Unified Three-Task Diffusion Network for End-to-End RGB-T Perception arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes TriDifNet, a diffusion-based network that jointly performs registration, fusion, and detection on misaligned infrared and visible image pairs. It uses three diffusion modules for alignment, fusion, and detection, linked by a closed-loop optimization scheme. Experiments on the KAIST multispectral pedestrian benchmark report superior detection performance under misaligned RGB-T settings.

entry.title: Learning to Look Beyond Screens: Transferable Visual Observation from GUI Grounding
entry.summary: Learning to Look Beyond Screens: Transferable Visual Observation from GUI Grounding arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper introduces LBS (Look Beyond Screens), a vision-language model first initialized with supervised training on teacher-generated GUI grounding trajectories. It is then trained with reinforcement learning to make multi-turn crop-and-inspect decisions. LBS consistently outperforms its baselines on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B and Qwen3.8-27B under fixed inference settings. The gains also transfer to PerceptionBench for both backbones and to HR-Bench and ChartQAPro for Qwen3.5-35B-A3B.

entry.title: Paper overview: why Direct Preference Optimization yields sparse weight updates
entry.summary: On the Sparsity of Direct Preference Optimization: Weight Disentanglement in the NTK Regime arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper theoretically explains why Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) produces sparse parameter updates. Analyzing DPO under a neural tangent kernel linearization, the authors show its logistic loss induces an implicit maximum-margin bias and introduce the notion of dual sparsity. Experiments on GPT-2 and several 7–9B instruction-tuned models confirm both sparsity sources, and on GPT-2 DPO reduces cross-task interference by up to 35 times compared with supervised fine-tuning.

entry.title: OpenGray: A Benchmark for Assessing Decisions of Radiotherapy Planning AI Agents
entry.summary: OpenGray: a benchmark for evaluating the decisions of radiotherapy planning agents arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper introduces OpenGray, a benchmark for testing whether large language model-based radiotherapy planning agents make correct decisions, such as when to submit a plan or request review. It adds tasks with known correct answers to the OpenKBP-Opt head-and-neck dataset, including contradictory dose goals and a feasible control task. The authors find that systems with favorable overall scores still made specific decision errors, particularly on contradictory cases. They conclude that planning agents should be evaluated on their decisions as well as dose and should have an explicit action for stopping and requesting review.

entry.title: SYMBA: Self-supervised brain MRI autoencoder for detecting neurodegenerative diseases
entry.summary: Systematic Morphometric Brain Autoencoding for Representation Learning in Neurodegenerative Diseases arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper introduces SYMBA, a self-supervised pretraining framework for structural brain MRI that uses anatomically constrained masking, an MS-SSIM reconstruction objective, and a curriculum moving from local detail to global morphology. It was pretrained on 6,953 T1-weighted scans from nine cohorts and evaluated with frozen linear probing on two unseen datasets. SYMBA reached 0.930 AUROC for Alzheimer's disease classification and 0.772 for mild cognitive impairment conversion, and about 0.90 AUROC for AD/CN classification using only six labeled subjects.

entry.title: Correctness Filtering as Selection Bias in Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness Evaluation
entry.summary: Correctness Conditioning as Selection in Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness Evaluation arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper argues that restricting chain-of-thought faithfulness evaluation to correctly answered instances changes the population being measured. Using a seven-variable structural causal model, the authors derive the exact observed gap and review 18 papers' protocols. Positive selection gaps appear across four arithmetic deployments, with the primary run showing a 7.4 percentage-point gap. The authors note that when counterfactual compliance is observable for every instance, all traces can be evaluated directly without correctness filtering.

entry.title: EnergyCal: Reducing Loss Spikes in Muon-Family Optimizers for Sparse MoE Training
entry.summary: EnergyCal: Taming Loss Spikes in Muon-Family Optimizers for Sparse MoE Training arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper introduces EnergyCal, a lightweight rule that scales down routed-expert updates based on the normalized squared Frobenius norm of their finite-step Newton-Schulz directions. It leaves the spectral transform unchanged and adds no persistent optimizer state. On a 4B-parameter MoE model, EnergyCal-MuonH cuts mean thresholded loss-spike burden by 99.51% and final geometric-mean perplexity by 4.06% compared with a lower-learning-rate MuonH recipe, at a modest throughput cost.

entry.title: Limits of the Delta Learning Hypothesis: Generator Biases in Single-Pair DPO Preference Data
entry.summary: Exploring the Limits of the Delta Learning Hypothesis: Single-Pair Generator Biases in Direct Preference Optimization arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper examines Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) when preference data comes from a single pair of models, treating the larger model's response as preferred. The authors show theoretically and empirically that fixed model pairs introduce generator-dependent biases that predict the preference label regardless of response quality. As a result, DPO trained on single-pair data consistently underperforms DPO trained on multi-model preference data.

entry.title: Quantized edge inference of a self-supervised SAR-optical encoder on ordinary x86 computers
entry.summary: Quantized Edge Inference of a Self-Supervised SAR-Optical Encoder on Commodity x86 Hardware arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper deploys a pretrained SAR-optical masked-autoencoder encoder on three commodity x86 machines and compares FP32, FP16 and INT8 precision for latency, energy and linear-probe accuracy. INT8 quantization leaves accuracy essentially unchanged. It lowers CPU latency on every machine and reduces CPU energy where measured.

entry.title: Learning to Code the World: Evolving Harnesses for Compositional 3D Reconstruction
entry.summary: Learning to Code the World: Harness Evolution for Compositional 3D Reconstruction arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents SceneEvolve, a framework that represents 3D scenes as executable code and improves reconstruction by evolving the harness around a small open-source agent. A stronger teacher agent iteratively refines the harness using feedback from development-set reconstructions, while model parameters, action semantics, and the execution backend stay fixed. On two in-domain datasets and one out-of-domain dataset, the method improves all four reconstruction metrics for the Qwen3.8-27B model and cuts mean inference time by 47.0% relative to the base model.

entry.title: AI-assisted discovery of CNOT decompositions for quantum permutations on constrained qubit topologies
entry.summary: AI-Assisted Discovery of CNOT Decompositions for Quantum Permutations on Constrained Topologies arXiv · Oct 27, 2026Limited qubit connectivity in quantum computers adds overhead when implementing logical operations. Using the AlphaCNOT tool, the authors find a decomposition for remote transpositions that uses at most 6d-4 CNOT gates for two qubits at graph distance d, compared with 6d-3 for the SWAP-based construction. They formalize this as Global Transpositions, a deterministic synthesis method for whole permutations, and identify an intermediate CNOT fusion mechanism.

entry.title: Guided-RLVR: Guided Exploration in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
entry.summary: Guided-RLVR: Guided Exploration in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes Guided-RLVR, an extension of reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) for improving LLM reasoning. Standard RLVR rollouts tend to collapse onto a narrow set of reasoning trajectories. The method adds a lightweight controller that injects semantically meaningful steering tokens into the sampling distribution, so the model approaches problems from multiple reasoning perspectives. Experiments on math reasoning and code generation benchmarks show it consistently outperforms existing RLVR methods and produces more diverse reasoning trajectories.

entry.title: Zooming without Zooming v2: Connecting Visual Evidence for More Generalizable Multimodal Perception
entry.summary: Zooming without Zooming v2: From Seeing Details to Connecting Evidence for Generalizable Multimodal Perception arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper introduces EvidenceConnect, a framework that synthesizes training questions from zoomed views of related regions within one image, requiring comparison, aggregation, or chaining of visual evidence. Reference answers are kept only when independent VLMs agree, and region-ablation tests remove questions whose answers survive region removal. Base VLMs trained on this data with RLVR, yielding ZwZ2, show gains in fine-grained and spatial perception and in several other tasks, even though the data were not tailored to any benchmark.

entry.title: GraftRay: Physically Consistent Mesh Insertion into Gaussian Splatting Scenes via Path Tracing
entry.summary: GraftRay: Physically Based Mesh Insertion into Gaussian Splatting Scenes via Path Tracing arXiv · Oct 27, 2026GraftRay is a method for inserting mesh objects into indoor scenes represented by 2D or 3D Gaussian Splatting while keeping lighting physically consistent. It estimates scene materials and surface normals using diffusion-based priors and models spatially extended light sources in closed form. A hybrid renderer path-traces the scene Gaussians together with the inserted meshes to produce view-consistent shading, interreflections, and soft shadows. On the FIPT benchmark, it outperforms baselines such as ComGS and EAG-PT in rendering fidelity and shadow accuracy while remaining highly efficient.

entry.title: A study comparing explainable deep learning models for breast cancer diagnosis from medical images
entry.summary: Interpretable Deep Learning Models for Breast Cancer Diagnosis Using Medical Imaging arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper benchmarks ten ImageNet-pretrained deep learning models for classifying benign versus malignant breast tumors on the BreakHis histopathology dataset, using a patient-level split. Predictions are explained with Grad-CAM, LIME, Integrated Gradients, and LRP. DenseNet121 performed best, reaching 99.4% test accuracy and an AUC-ROC of 0.999, while Transformer-based models trailed the CNNs.

entry.title: Comparing Regression Models for Predicting Crop Yield
entry.summary: Crop Yield Prediction Using Regression Models: A Comparative Evaluation of Model Performance arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This study compares five regression models for predicting crop yield from environmental, crop, and farm management variables. The dataset contained about one million observations, and models were tested with 80:20 and 70:30 train-test splits. Performance was measured by R-squared, mean squared error, and root mean squared error. Linear-type models performed competitively and similarly, while random forest showed a large gap between training and testing performance.

entry.title: Ground-to-Satellite Knowledge Distillation for Crop Classification Under Shift
entry.summary: Ground-to-Satellite Knowledge Distillation for Crop Classification under Temporal and Geographic Shift arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies whether ground-level field photographs can improve crop classification based on pretrained satellite embeddings. A teacher model using frozen CLIP features supervises classifiers trained on AlphaEarth and TESSERA representations, with photographs used only during training. On a paired dataset of 17 crop classes, distillation improves over satellite-only classification, with gains of up to +5.5 macro-F1 points under temporal shift and larger gains in geographic holdouts.

entry.title: V-LUMEN: Visual Lookup Memory for Scaling Embeddings in Vision-Language Models
entry.summary: V-LUMEN: Visual Lookup Memory for Embedding Scaling in Vision-Language Models arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper introduces V-LUMEN, a visual lookup memory for vision-language models that adds external memory instead of increasing model size. It discretizes visual features with a frozen codebook, builds spatially aware memory keys by hashing, modulates them with text-conditioned relevance signals, and fuses retrieved embeddings into the backbone through a gated residual pathway. On five reasoning-intensive benchmarks it improves a frozen Qwen3-VL-2B backbone and transfers zero-shot to three benchmarks whose images are disjoint from the training data. ★★★★ Notable: The authors bring lookup-based external memory to VLMs, using spatial hashing and gated residual fusion; the abstract reports gains on five reasoning benchmarks for a frozen Qwen3-VL-2B and zero-shot

entry.title: Testing Priority Dispatch for Premium Members in Shared On-demand Taxis
entry.summary: Evaluating Priority Dispatch for Premium Membership in On-demand Taxi-sharing arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper examines whether premium membership can be added to an on-demand taxi-sharing service at the dispatch level, using a sequential optimal insertion method. Two approaches are proposed: shortening deadlines for premium users, and shortening deadlines while using dedicated premium vehicles. Both are compared with a baseline dispatch method through SUMO simulations under steady, peak-period, and urban-concentrated demand. The results indicate that the suitable priority mechanism depends on operating conditions and the premium ratio, so switching methods by condition may benefit premium users while limiting the burden on non-premium users.

entry.title: From Ethernet to Wi-Fi: A Method for Choosing Features to Classify Network Traffic
entry.summary: From Ethernet to Wi-Fi: Flow Feature Selection and Construction for Traffic Classification arXiv · Oct 27, 2026Traffic classifiers trained on Ethernet data can lose accuracy on Wi-Fi traffic. The paper proposes a five-stage procedure for selecting and constructing flow features so that models trained only on Ethernet data can classify Wi-Fi flows. Ethernet and Wi-Fi traffic are simulated in ns-3, with Wi-Fi using the Best Effort access category. Labelled Wi-Fi data from six development scenarios guide feature design, and a separate scenario is reserved for final testing.

entry.title: Compote: A Collapse-Resistant Multi-Hypothesis Method for Sequential Recommendation
entry.summary: Compote: Collapse-Resistant Multiple Hypothesis Learning For Sequential Recommendation arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper addresses the ambiguity of next-item prediction in sequential recommendation by proposing COMPOTE, a multi-hypothesis transformer trained with an annealed objective that shifts from uniform supervision to winner-takes-all assignment, so hypotheses specialize in distinct catalogue regions. Using item IDs alone, it outperforms strong ID-based, generative, and multi-interest baselines on three Amazon Reviews 2023 benchmarks. Matched-capacity ablations attribute the gains to the annealed objective rather than extra capacity, ensembling, or routing.

entry.title: Meta-models: models that predict how other models learn
entry.summary: Meta Models: Models that Model Learning arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies meta-models, which predict the training behavior of other models. Treating language-model training records as numeric data, the authors find that the off-the-shelf tabular in-context learner TabPFN matches or outperforms a fine-tuned LLM meta-model in several evaluated settings, while needing only seconds of fit-and-predict time. Augmenting TabPFN with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) further improves accuracy on selected tasks, and the authors pre-registered a forecast for a large public training run.

entry.title: GPA-VGGT: A Training-Free Way to Speed Up VGGT While Keeping Geometric Accuracy
entry.summary: GPA-VGGT: Geometry-Preserving Acceleration of VGGT arXiv · Oct 27, 2026VGGT is a feed-forward model that recovers camera parameters, depth maps, and point maps from one to hundreds of views in a single pass. Its global attention cost grows quadratically with the number of frames, which makes long sequences slow. GPA-VGGT accelerates it without retraining by using frame attention with shared cross-frame keys and values in early blocks, merging only keys and values in later blocks, and randomly projecting the matching metric to 128 dimensions. The paper reports speedups comparable to prior work while retaining over 99% of VGGT's pose accuracy under AUC@3.

entry.title: Online gas classification at the edge: a low-power, insect-inspired neural network
entry.summary: Online gas classification at the edge arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents a neural network inspired by the insect olfactory system that classifies raw gas sensor array readings using a sparse, high-dimensional binary representation. It uses only binary weights and Hebbian local learning, making it suited to ultra-low-power neuromorphic processors. In a hazardous gas detection experiment on the mixed-signal neuromorphic chip TEXEL, the on-chip classifier reached 74.6% accuracy at 482 nJ per inference and 27 μW static power.

entry.title: CaLLM: Continual Adaptation of LLMs via Non-Parametric Adapter Routing
entry.summary: CaLLM: Continual Adaptation of LLMs via Non-Parametric Adapter Routing arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents CaLLM, a framework for continually adapting large language models to changing task distributions while reducing catastrophic forgetting. It combines metric-based meta-learning with modular parameter isolation using lightweight adapters, routing each input batch to the adapter matching its nearest prototype in a task-agnostic embedding space. The authors report that CaLLM outperforms traditional isolation and replay methods across diverse fine-grained continual learning benchmarks.

entry.title: SpectRAG: Graph-Based Context Selection for Multi-Hop Retrieval-Augmented Generation
entry.summary: SpectRAG: Weighted Chunk Graphs for Token-Budgeted Context Selection in Multi-Hop Retrieval-Augmented Generation arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes SpectRAG, a retrieval framework for retrieval-augmented generation that builds a weighted graph over document chunks and uses spectral relevance propagation. It expands candidate passages over this graph and assembles a context within a fixed token budget. Experiments on several datasets report improved evidence recovery and generation quality competitive with baselines, along with trade-offs in early precision and computational cost.

entry.title: The State of Multilingual LLM Evaluation: An Audit of 51 Benchmarks
entry.summary: The State and Fate of Multilingual, Contextual Evaluation in the NLP World arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper audits 51 recent multilingual benchmarks covering 242 datasets and 219 languages, examining coverage, representativeness, and rigor. It finds that many languages appear in only one benchmark, low-resource languages are evaluated on far fewer task categories, and 56% of dataset-language instances are translated from English. The authors also report benchmark contamination. They conclude with recommendations for natively constructed, culturally grounded, contamination-aware evaluation frameworks. ★★★★ Notable: The authors audit 51 multilingual benchmarks (242 datasets, 219 languages), reporting thin coverage, translation-dominated construction, and contamination, and propose recommendations for better evalu

entry.title: A testbed game for studying self-governing groups of humans and AI agents
entry.summary: A Serious-Game Testbed for Self-Governing Human-Machine Institutions arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper introduces Megabike, a multi-agent simulator and serious game for studying whether mixed human-machine groups can govern themselves. Riders sharing a megabike must agree on steering, pedalling and resource distribution, and choose their political regime. In forty sessions with language-model riders, the agents chose regimes, elected leaders and expelled one another. The results show that different combinations of agent types can produce unexpected and counterproductive outcomes.

entry.title: LearnPrunerV2: A Learnable Method for Gradually Removing Visual Tokens in Vision-Language Models
entry.summary: LearnPrunerV2: Learnable Progressive Token Pruning for Vision-Language Models arXiv · Oct 27, 2026Vision-language models process many visual tokens, which makes them computationally expensive. This paper proposes LearnPrunerV2, which adds lightweight learnable modules to every layer to score token importance by combining visual saliency with query relevance. It also introduces Budget-Deterministic Pruning, a fixed per-layer schedule based on a staircase redundancy pattern. The authors report that on LLaVA-v1.5 it keeps 99.8% of the original performance while pruning 77.8% of visual tokens.

entry.title: Advancement or Acceleration? How Data Curation Improves LLM Training
entry.summary: Advancement or Acceleration? How Data Curation Improves LLM Training arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper distinguishes two effects of data curation for LLM training: advancement, which raises the performance a model can ultimately reach, and acceleration, which reaches the same performance with less data. The authors propose a Δ-test, the gap between the uncurated baseline's training and target losses, which can be computed before curation. In experiments, a clearly nonzero Δ predicts persistent gains, while gains near Δ=0 tend to shrink as the training budget grows.

entry.title: Neural network-guided road network reduction for city-wide centralized traffic routing
entry.summary: GNN-Guided Network Reduction for Centralized Urban Traffic Routing arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies centralized traffic routing, where a central planner assigns routes to origin-destination vehicle flows to minimize congestion-dependent segment costs. The authors propose a learning-based network reduction method: a graph neural network scores road segments for each OD flow, highly ranked segments are assembled into complete routes, and the original segment-flow MILP is solved on the reduced network. Experiments on four real urban networks show the smallest relative objective difference to a 30-second full-graph reference in every city under both traffic regimes, and traffic simulations indicate more efficient routing.

entry.title: AutoVend: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Long-Term Autonomous Vending Machine Operations
entry.summary: AutoVend: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Autonomous Vending Operations arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper introduces AutoVend, a benchmark where one LLM agent manages 20 vending machines across five site types through a Web interface over 180 simulated days. The simulator includes a shared warehouse, procurement lead times, paid replenishment, inventory expiration, and recurring operating costs. Four of the five evaluated LLM agents underperform a rule-based inventory-control baseline, and inventory and execution costs often erode gains in individual metrics.

entry.title: Explicit Regional Maps for Judging Video Quality
entry.summary: Explicit Regional Representations For Video Quality Assessment arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper addresses the problem that end-to-end video quality assessment methods leave their regional evidence largely implicit. The authors introduce a Quality-Relevance Heatmap (QRH), a pixel-level explicit regional representation that combines localized degradation evidence with perceptual priors under vision-language model guidance, without requiring pixel-level annotations. Applied to the DOVER model through two deterministic fragment-sampling strategies, the quality-aware sampling variant improves most evaluated metrics on popular VQA benchmarks.

entry.title: VC dimension of autoregressive linear threshold functions
entry.summary: On the VC Dimension of Autoregressive Linear Threshold Functions arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies the VC dimension of autoregressive linear threshold functions, a class of Boolean predictors that repeatedly apply a linear threshold to the most recent d bits and return the bit produced after T steps. The authors prove that for deterministic autoregressive LTFs the VC dimension is Θ(d²) for every T ≥ d², resolving a known quadratic gap. They also adapt the technique to show that replacing the sign function with logistic sampling can raise the VC dimension of the final majority prediction class from quadratic to exponential in d.

entry.title: Paper on a memory method that helps event-driven AI agents act proactively
entry.summary: Proactive Memory for Event-Driven LLM Agents arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes ProactMem, a memory method that organizes history into recent events, temporal trajectories, and behavioral regularities. Trajectory facts are checked against source events, and regularities are validated by historical replay before being matched to current conditions. The authors also build ProactiveStream, a longitudinal benchmark across three application scopes, where ProactMem reaches an overall F1 of 52.6%, a 21.4% relative gain over the strongest of five baselines.

entry.title: Do bots feel bad? Reviewing evidence for functional valence in LLMs
entry.summary: Do bots feel bad? Assessing empirical evidence for functional valence in LLMs arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper examines whether large language models have valenced states, meaning states that feel pleasant or unpleasant. It assesses recent claims of functional pleasure, pain, and emotions in LLMs against the philosophical and cognitive science understanding of valence. The author argues that key aspects of valence remain untested and that current experiments fail to separate functional valence from preferences, value judgments, and role-play. The paper closes by proposing new experimental approaches aimed at valence itself.

entry.title: Live-OPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Proactive Streaming Video Assistants
entry.summary: Live-OPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Proactive Streaming Large Video Models arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper introduces Live-OPSD, a training method for streaming multimodal assistants that must decide when and how to respond while video events are still unfolding. It uses hints available only during training to guide the model on its own generated outputs. On Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B, Live-OPSD scores 59.64 on LiveProBench, 5.26 points above the strongest continued-SFT baseline, and 65.84 on OVO-Bench.

entry.title: PailitaoMMSearch2.0 Technical Report: Scaling Generative Retrieval to Unified End-to-End Multimodal Search
entry.summary: PailitaoMMSearch2.0 Technical Report: Scaling Generative Retrieval to Unified End-to-End Multimodal Search arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents PailitaoMMSearch, a system that generates product Semantic IDs directly from a raw query image and free-form instruction, aiming for unified end-to-end multimodal search. It scales along data, intent, and scenario dimensions, using continual pre-training, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning. The system is deployed in Taobao Pailitao, and a controlled online A/B test reports statistically significant gains in item page views, transactions, and gross merchandise value. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes PailitaoMMSearch, a unified end-to-end multimodal system generating product Semantic IDs from query images and instructions; the authors report Taobao A/B gains of +17.90% page views, +27.04%

entry.title: Dense learning and differentiable shape modeling for detecting spine landmarks in X-rays
entry.summary: Dense Representation Learning and Differentiable Shape Modeling for Spine Landmark Detection arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper treats spine landmark detection in spinal X-rays as a pixel-level contrastive representation learning problem, matching dense pixel embeddings to landmark prototypes. Even with a generic U-Net backbone, it produces more discriminative heatmaps than traditional heatmap regression, improving discrimination between vertebral corners on different vertebrae. The heatmaps are combined with learnable shape priors over the global configuration of spinal landmarks to resolve location ambiguities. The approach is competitive in landmark accuracy and clinical parameter estimation on the public AASCE dataset and two private spinal X-ray datasets.

entry.title: DCKV: A trained codec that compresses prompt KV caches in hybrid language models.
entry.summary: DCKV: Learned Transform Coding of the Prompt KV Cache in Hybrid Language Models arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents DCKV, a differentiable codec for the key-value cache of hybrid language models and described as the first such codec trained end to end. Its transform, quantizer and entropy models are conditioned on prompt tokens and already decoded neighbouring positions, and are optimized jointly against the frozen language model. On Qwen3.5-2B, DCKV stores a compressed token in more than 55 times fewer bytes than bf16 with at most a 1.8-point loss on three long-context benchmarks, and in more than 100 times fewer bytes with at most a 3.6-point loss.

entry.title: Remembering dialogue inside a frozen language model's parameters, without external memory
entry.summary: Self-Keyed In-Parameter Memorization for External Memory-Free Dialogue Recall in Frozen Language Models arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper asks whether a language model can store a dialogue inside its own parameters and later answer questions about it, with no external memory. The proposed method, SKIM, has the model generate its own varied questions for each dialogue turn and write them into its parameters as keys for retrieving that turn's content. Evaluated on five language models, SKIM recalls most stored dialogue turns from later user questions, answering from the parameters alone.

entry.title: Beyond QASecClaw: Agent Scaling and Evidence Reliability in Software Assurance
entry.summary: Beyond QASecClaw: Agent Scaling, Verifier Feedback, and Evidence Reliability in Software Assurance arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper asks whether adding specialist language-model contexts improves software assurance when deterministic tool evidence is already available. The authors run five experiments covering Java warning controls, OWASP Benchmark, Defects4J test generation, SV-COMP verdicts, and misleading evidence packages. Increasing context count sharply raises token use without improving unsafe clearance, while verifier feedback and verdict aggregation show mixed results. The findings support deterministic evidence admission in the tested settings and expose limits in feedback interpretation and evaluation coverage.

entry.title: Algorithmic monoculture risks in machine learning fertilizer recommendations
entry.summary: Algorithmic Monoculture in Machine Learning-based Site-Specific Fertilizer Recommendation arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper argues that machine learning fertilizer recommendations are usually evaluated one model at a time, yet correlated errors can accumulate across interconnected farms and create systemic costs. It models social loss from shared and farm-specific errors, using the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index and a covariance-generalized formulation to analyze model concentration and error dependence. Calibrated on nine model families across five Moroccan cereal systems, it finds that accuracy-constrained diversification lowers modeled social loss by 10.89-41.53% under a 10% regret cap, though these counterfactual results are not agronomic or monetary welfare estimates.

entry.title: TDLM: Adaptive Temporal Integration for Diffusion Language Models
entry.summary: TDLM: Adaptive Temporal Integration for Diffusion Language Models arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper introduces TDLM, a temporal self-conditioning diffusion language model that lets unresolved token positions attend to their own history of hidden representations inside a frozen denoiser. Training uses self-generated trajectories and a cross-entropy objective, with causal temporal attention enabling parallel evaluation. On LLaDA and Dream, the main comparison reports up to 7.15 times faster generation than the original models, with competitive answer quality on the evaluated tasks.

entry.title: JevRec: Variable-length item codes for LLM-based recommendation
entry.summary: JevRec: Linguistic Encoding with Jev-like Decision Modeling for LLM-based Generative Recommendation arXiv · Oct 27, 2026JevRec is a generative recommendation method using LLMs that encodes items as variable-length semantic identifiers, giving popular items shorter codes and long-tail items richer ones. It uses separate output heads to predict the code length and the code content, sharing the interaction-history representation. The authors report that it outperforms all compared baselines on three public datasets, with lower training and inference time than TIGER.

entry.title: Gaussian process bandit method for optimizing constrained black-box allocation levers
entry.summary: Gaussian Process Bandits for Constraint Black Box Lever Optimization arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper addresses how to optimize discrete budget allocation weights across segments when feedback is delayed, noisy, aggregated, and weight changes are rate-limited. It proposes a GP-UCB approach that places a Gaussian process prior on the reward function so neighboring configurations share information. A synthetic simulator identifies a composite Matérn plus Linear kernel as the most robust across stationary, drifting, and reactive settings. A large randomized controlled trial in production reports a statistically significant efficiency gain over an ε-greedy baseline.

entry.title: Detecting Provenance of LoRA-Adapted Image Diffusion Models
entry.summary: Provenance Signatures for Low Rank Adaptations of Image Diffusion Models arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes a protocol for determining whether an online service is using a Low Rank Adaptation (LoRA) version of a standard image diffusion model. It considers an open-world setting in which the possible adaptations and alternative models are unknown. Using hypothesis testing, the method builds a black-box signature based only on the intrinsic dimension of sets of generated images, distinguishing the base model, LoRA adaptations, and entirely different model families.

entry.title: DocXEval: A Systematic Evaluation of Explainability in Multimodal Document Understanding
entry.summary: DocXEval: A Systematic Evaluation of Explainability in Multimodal Document Understanding arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper introduces DocXEval, a comprehensive explainability framework for multimodal document understanding that combines text, layout, and image. It adapts existing explainable AI methods and metrics to this setting and adds multi-target variants for tasks such as semantic entity recognition. The authors evaluate 13 XAI methods across 3 tasks, 8 datasets, 4 models, and 17 metrics, finding that Occlusion is the most faithful and interpretable overall. The work also includes a meta-evaluation of metrics and dataset-wide analyses of model behavior. ★★★★ Notable: First XAI framework for multimodal document understanding, systematically evaluating 13 methods and 17 metrics across 8 datasets and 4 models; the authors report Occlusion as most faithful overall.

entry.title: Vision-language agents that learn inside their own latent world
entry.summary: Vision-Language Agents Can Learn in Their Own Latent Worlds arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper introduces Dwell, a model-based reinforcement learning framework that treats a pretrained vision-language model as a recurrent latent transition operator. The agent predicts, adjusts, and acts in latent space, learning from both real interactions and latent imagination. The authors report that across five interactive visual environments, Dwell achieves the strongest overall performance among trainable methods while substantially reducing imagination compute.

entry.title: Can Lightweight Decision Models Classify Why Retrieved Sources Conflict in RAG?
entry.summary: Do We Need an LLM to Know Why Sources Conflict? Decision Models for Knowledge-Conflict Typing in RAG arXiv · Oct 27, 2026When retrieved sources disagree, the appropriate response depends on the type of conflict. This paper tests whether decision models, which output probabilities over fixed options in a single forward pass, can classify conflict types quickly and cheaply. On the CONFLICTS benchmark, 10 of 11 decision models match or exceed Gemini 2.5 Flash (61.3%) in accuracy, at 4 to 39 times lower billed cost. ★★★★ Notable: The authors apply decision models to RAG knowledge-conflict typing on CONFLICTS, comparing them with Gemini models and cascades; they report most match or beat Gemini 2.5 Flash accuracy at lower cost

entry.title: Building a Basque Speech Language Model for Spoken Conversation
entry.summary: Developing a Speech Language Model for Basque arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents the first open speech language model for Basque, designed for low-latency, end-to-end spoken interaction. It builds on the LLaMA-Omni architecture with a Latxa backbone, fine-tuning several modules to carry Basque language ability into speech. To address data scarcity, the English VoiceAssistant-400K corpus was translated into Basque and synthesized with a Basque TTS system. Reported results are 3.86/5 for content quality, 9.94% WER for intelligibility, and 3.07 UTMOS for audio quality.

entry.title: Nothing Left Behind: Finding Evidence in Large Trial Collections
entry.summary: Nothing Left Behind: Finding Evidence from a Large Randomized Evaluation Corpus arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper compares two ways to find relevant evidence in a large collection: tagging items with labels and searching on them, versus using text embeddings to find candidates by meaning and then having a language model keep only the relevant ones. In a corpus of 7,354 randomized trials, label search found 45% of the evidence a systematic review would include, while the new approach found 92%. The authors propose a two-stage architecture that combines broad candidate retrieval with query-specific evidence filtering.

entry.title: HiLo-RD: Cross-Budget Self-Distillation for Masked Diffusion Language Models
entry.summary: HiLo-RD: Cross-Budget Self-Distillation for Masked Diffusion Language Models arXiv · Oct 27, 2026HiLo-RD is a method that improves masked diffusion language models under a limited generation budget. It pairs states from a large-window teacher with cropped small-window views and matches their hidden representations at committed positions, guiding both token prediction and commitment order. On mathematics benchmarks it raises low-budget accuracy and shortens responses, and on GSM8K accuracy rises by 9.4 percentage points while mean readable length falls by about 25%.

entry.title: Mining natural hard negatives from positives for instruction-following retrieval
entry.summary: Natural Hard-Negative Mining from Positives for Instruction-Following Retrieval arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper addresses the scarcity of instruction-conditioned contrastive supervision for instruction-following information retrieval. It proposes Natural Hard-Negative Mining (NHNM), which turns original positive passages into instruction hard negatives and builds high-contrast training data through automated candidate cleaning, reversal construction, and geometry filtering. Applied to MSMARCO, it yields NHNM-MARCO, a training set of nearly 7K instances, and models of 568M to 4B parameters fine-tuned on it perform strongly on InstructIR and FollowIR, matching or surpassing much larger retrievers in several settings.

entry.title: PREEN: Color style transfer by predicting smartphone editor presets from a reference
entry.summary: PREEN: Exemplar-Based Color Style Transfer with Smartphone Editor Presets arXiv · Oct 27, 2026PREEN treats color style transfer as predicting the 29 slider values of a deterministic image editor, producing an editor preset instead of a raster image. It trains with pseudo-presets obtained by inverting a style-transfer teacher's outputs into the editor's parameter space, then refines a CLIP-conditioned regressor with LoRA. On the PST50 benchmark it leads baselines on pixel and perceptual fidelity metrics, and a single inference-time strength knob moves continuously from the default look to a vivid one.

entry.title: Noise Steering: a reinforcement learning method that uses turbine yaw to limit wind farm noise while keeping power output high
entry.summary: Noise Steering: Exploiting Wake Steering and Acoustic Directivity for Noise-Constrained Wind Farm Control via Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes Noise Steering, a model-free reinforcement learning strategy that jointly controls turbine yaw angles and power setpoints to maximise farm power under a local noise constraint. Training uses a low-fidelity acoustic model coupled with the steady-state FLORIS simulator. On a six-turbine test farm, the policy satisfies a 40 dB noise limit across turbulent winds with an average power deficit of about 2%, compared with 17% for the industry-standard noise-reduced operation baseline.

entry.title: Joint Neural Architecture and Hyperparameter Search via Evolutionary Optimization for Reinforcement Learning (HPNAS-RL)
entry.summary: Hyperparameter and Neural Architecture Search via Evolutionary Optimization for Reinforcement Learning: HPNAS-RL arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes a dual-branch evolutionary framework that simultaneously performs neural architecture search and hyperparameter optimization for reinforcement learning in autonomous driving. It builds on the authors' earlier EMNAS method, evolving discrete network architectures and continuous hyperparameters in parallel under a unified multi-objective strategy, with parallel evaluation and teacher-student policy transfer. Experiments in a high-fidelity driving simulator show that the joint approach outperforms standalone NAS, yielding policies with higher rewards, fewer parameters, and improved stability.

entry.title: RAG-CSI: Global-Local Retrieval for CSI Prediction via Joint State and Dynamics Matching
entry.summary: RAG-CSI: Global Local Retrieval via Joint State and Dynamics Matching for CSI Prediction arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes RAG-CSI, a retrieval-enhanced Transformer that predicts future channel state information (CSI) from historical observations. It builds a global-local CSI knowledge store and uses joint state-dynamics retrieval (JSDR) to find relevant CSI sequences, which a cross-attention Transformer fuses with the current CSI history. On a multi-scene CSI dataset, it improves all five evaluation metrics by over 10% relative to the best baseline for each, including a 15.42% reduction in normalized mean squared error.

entry.title: RubricAtlas: Type-level scoring criteria mined from expert reports to evaluate deep research agents
entry.summary: RubricAtlas: Mining Type-Level Rubrics from Expert Reports to Evaluate Deep Research Agents arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper introduces RubricAtlas, which derives type-level analytical requirements from expert reports on different objects within the same research type and links binary checkpoints to report passages. Built from 3,079 Chinese financial research reports covering 99 research types, it finds that individual reports cover only about half of their type's analytical questions. Across ten agents, two judge pipelines show checkpoint agreement of κ = 0.71 and agent-ranking agreement of Kendall τ = 0.87.

entry.title: GUI-JEPA: A Fast, Decoder-Free Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents Using JEPA Latents
entry.summary: GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latents as a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper introduces GUI-JEPA, a decoder-free action policy for mobile GUI agents built on a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture. It selects actions in the latent space of an encoder pretrained on unlabelled GUI screenshots, using an action- and region-conditioned predictor to score all candidate actions in one batched pass. On AndroidControl, it is reported to run 2.8-4.0x faster than a fine-tuned Qwen2.5-VL-7B agent, using 6% of its parameters while reaching 86-92% of its in-distribution accuracy. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes a decoder-free mobile GUI policy scoring actions in JEPA latent space; the authors report 2.8-4.0x speedup over a same-input fine-tuned 7B VLM on AndroidControl, with 6% of parameters and 86-

entry.title: HoloRecon: Globally Consistent Long-Range Panorama Reconstruction
entry.summary: HoloRecon: Incremental Reconstruction of Long-Range Panoramas with Global Consistency arXiv · Oct 27, 2026HoloRecon is a framework that combines an ORB-based sparse panoramic mapping frontend with a fine-tuned feed-forward model to reconstruct long panoramic sequences. The predicted local geometry is used to verify feature matches across distant revisits, providing long-range camera constraints that optimize the global pose graph. The authors also introduce PanoRecon, a seven-scene benchmark with repetitive architecture and reference poses and LiDAR geometry. The method achieves the lowest mean absolute trajectory error and a high F-1 score among the evaluated methods.

entry.title: RangeRectQuant: Compressing Scientific Maps So Any Future Rectangle Sum Stays Accurate
entry.summary: RangeRectQuant: Compressing Scientific Fields for Every Future Rectangular Sum arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents RangeRectQuant, a method for compressing scientific raster data so that the sum over any axis-aligned rectangle remains within a prescribed error budget. It controls errors in prefix sums during encoding, so users can later measure arbitrary rectangles without the source data or re-encoding. The method runs in linear time and needs workspace of about one row. Experiments on geographically held-out built-surface and water-occurrence maps show substantial storage savings over alternatives meeting the same requirements.

entry.title: Tail Cues, Principal Corrections: A Lightweight Plug-and-Play Fix for Open-Set Test-Time Adaptation
entry.summary: Tail Cues, Principal Corrections: Plug-and-Play Rectification for Open-Set Test-Time Adaptation arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper addresses open-set test-time adaptation, where target data streams contain both covariate and semantic shifts. It introduces TALOR, a lightweight, backward-free module that uses the source linear head as a geometric anchor to split features into principal and tail coordinates. TALOR estimates an affine correction in the principal subspace via weighted ridge regression and uses it to rectify features before the source head. On ImageNet-C with six csOOD datasets, it outperforms the next-best UniEnt by 2.2% H-score while running 2.5x faster and using 12% of its GPU memory.

entry.title: Sample-and-Score: Surrogate-Guided Coordinated Spatial Reuse in IEEE 802.11
entry.summary: Sample-and-Score: Surrogate-Guided Coordinated Spatial Reuse in IEEE 802.11 Networks arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper addresses coordinated spatial reuse (Co-SR) in IEEE 802.11bn, where multiple access points transmit simultaneously to raise area throughput, a task hampered by a large combinatorial configuration space. The authors propose a sample-and-score method that randomly draws Co-SR configurations, scores each with a surrogate model, and selects the best. The surrogate is trained offline and deployed without online fine-tuning or sequential exploration. On unseen topologies with 2 to 16 access points, it recovers 52% to 77% of a perfect surrogate's throughput, and a perfect sample-and-score approach reaches 95% of the upper bound with 8192 candidates.

entry.title: Intrinsic Information-Theoretic Analysis of ReLU Nets
entry.summary: Intrinsic Information-Theoretic Analysis of ReLU Nets arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies how mutual information in deep networks can be analysed without the bias of external estimators, by using the piecewise-linear structure of ReLU-type networks that partitions inputs into linear regions. It decomposes mutual information into geometric terms, with the dominant routing information having a plug-in estimator. The estimator agrees strongly with three established baselines, and a functional-equivalence quotient restores informative estimates when the partition saturates.

entry.title: HorizON: A multi-horizon neural network for predicting how organic battery stacks perform over time.
entry.summary: HorizON: A Multi-Horizon Deep Operator Network for Property Prediction of Organic Battery Stacks arXiv · Oct 27, 2026Organic electrode materials can reduce reliance on critical metals like lithium, cobalt, and nickel, but organic batteries still have limited long-term cycling stability. The paper introduces HorizON, a multi-fidelity, multi-horizon Deep Operator Network that learns DFT redox potentials and cycle-dependent specific-capacity trajectories within one model. It is trained on complete battery-stack representations and usage conditions so it captures interactions among stack components, not just the cathode. The framework is presented for long-term property prediction, inverse design, and process optimization of organic battery systems.

entry.title: ActiveAlign: Aligning Robot Manipulation Through Active Perception
entry.summary: ActiveAlign: Aligning Egocentric Manipulation via Active Perception arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes ActiveAlign, a framework that uses active perception, such as moving the hand and touching objects, to close the gap between real-world and simulated environments. ActiveAlign-Waving performs hand-eye calibration using active hand motions and differentiable rendering, while ActiveAlign-Touching refines object alignment with tactile feedback to reach millimeter-level precision. The authors show that the method can curate simulation environments for uncalibrated robot datasets and enables a Unitree G1 robot to manipulate millimeter-scale objects such as pressing buttons and moving sliders.

entry.title: Switchable unlearning that removes training data while keeping retrieval ability.
entry.summary: Forget the Data, Keep the Capability: Switchable Unlearning for Retrieval arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper presents MoME, a framework that lets one model switch between Full mode for standard inference and Core mode for unlearned inference, supporting privacy requests to delete individuals' training data. Core parameters receive no gradients from the forget set, making Core independent of that data, and the authors introduce the Forgetting-Rank statistic to audit this independence. On Market-1501, VeRi-776, and RegDB, Core performs near a retrained reference under three membership attacks while retrieving above it. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose MoME, a switchable framework with gradient-isolated branches enabling unlearning, prove Core is independent of the forget set up to coupling channels, and report retrieval above a

entry.title: Testing AlphaEarth embeddings for crop classification across separability, time, and regions
entry.summary: Evaluating AlphaEarth Embeddings for Crop Classification: Separability, Temporal Dynamics, and Cross-Regional Transferability arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes a representation-agnostic framework to compare 64-dimensional AlphaEarth embeddings from a geospatial foundation model against Sentinel-2 reflectance, NDVI phenology, and harmonic features for crop classification. The evaluation uses field-scale data from the conterminous US (2017–2023) and Northern India (2021). Embeddings give better distribution-aware separation and capture multi-year crop rotation, while harmonic and NDVI features transfer better from the US to India, and the combined feature space performs in a balanced way.

entry.title: How boundary shape sets the best shallow ReLU approximation rate under weight limits
entry.summary: Boundary Geometry Determines Optimal Shallow ReLU Approximation under Weighted Coefficient Constraints arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies how the boundary shape of a convex body affects approximation of functions by shallow ReLU neural networks in the L^q norm. The target classes are unit balls of weighted variation spaces, which extend classical spaces by building domain geometry into constraints on output coefficients. The authors give upper and lower bounds for arbitrary convex bodies and determine optimal exponents for planar convex bodies and their products with polytopes, including cubes and cylinders. They show that boundary geometry can change the optimal exponent even when dimension, error norm, and weighting rule are fixed.

entry.title: LingGS: Separating Feed-Forward Geometry Prediction from Camera Tracking for High-Fidelity Gaussian SLAM
entry.summary: LingGS: Decoupling Feed-Forward Geometry Prediction from Camera Tracking for High-Fidelity Gaussian SLAM arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents an online monocular RGB Gaussian splatting SLAM system that uses a frozen streaming 3D foundation model as a virtual RGB-D sensor for depth estimation. An explicit geometric solver estimates camera motion via feature reprojection, and a streaming Gaussian mapper integrates observations into a dense scene representation. The authors report improved reconstruction quality on indoor and outdoor datasets, about 7 FPS on a single RTX 4090, and 2-3 times the throughput of evaluated prior SLAM systems.

entry.title: uTHCD-C: A Robustness Benchmark for Tamil Handwritten Character Recognition under Corruptions
entry.summary: uTHCD-C: A Corruption-Robustness Benchmark for Tamil Handwritten Character Recognition arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper introduces uTHCD-C, a benchmark for testing how well Tamil handwritten character recognition systems withstand image corruptions. Built on the unconstrained Tamil Handwritten Character Database (uTHCD), it defines ten corruption types, including a handwriting-specific stroke-thinning corruption, at five severity levels. Nine convolutional and transformer-based architectures are compared using mean Corruption Error normalized to VGG16-BN. ConvNeXt and Swin achieved the lowest mCE values (0.75 and 0.83), while ShuffleNet and MnasNet showed higher values (1.55 and 1.85).

entry.title: When All Rollouts Fail: Policy-Compatible Joint Decoding for Hard Problems
entry.summary: When All Rollouts Fail: Policy-Compatible Joint Decoding for Hard-Problem Reasoning arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper addresses a problem in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, where models get no learning signal on problems beyond their current ability because every attempt fails. It proposes PICO, which uses distribution-constrained joint decoding so expert data guides generation while staying compatible with the current policy. These trajectories are optimized together with on-policy rollouts using a mixed-behavior objective. Experiments on diverse reasoning datasets and agentic benchmarks show PICO outperforms standard RLVR and prior off-policy baselines.

entry.title: Evolving Agent Teams: A Multi-Agent Framework Escaping Local Optima
entry.summary: Evolving Agent Teams arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper finds that existing coding agents converge to local optima when optimizing real-world expert-written GPU kernels such as FlashInfer. The authors propose Evolving Agent Teams, in which a central supervisor diagnoses local optima and restructures the agent team, while a persistent file system stores accumulated experience. With an extended token budget, the generated CUDA kernel reaches a 1.2x mean speedup over the production FlashInfer MLA paged decode kernel and wins on 36 of 47 FlashInfer-Bench workloads. ★★★★ Notable: A central supervisor diagnoses local optima and restructures agent teams, using a persistent file system to accumulate experience; the authors report speedups on real FlashInfer kernel and other tasks

entry.title: A conservative policy iteration method for zero-sum partially observable games
entry.summary: Conservative Policy Iteration For Zero-Sum POSGs arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents an approximate policy-iteration algorithm for finite-horizon zero-sum partially observable stochastic games (zs-POSGs). It keeps one policy per player and updates both along occupancy trajectories produced by conservative policy updates, using a single supporting hyperplane from the current joint policy instead of a full central value function. On finite-horizon zero-sum POSG benchmarks, it is competitive at small horizons and often gives a better runtime-exploitability trade-off at larger horizons than PBVI, HSVI, and CFR+.

entry.title: AxisQ: Depth-Adaptive Channel-Frequency Quantization for Camouflaged Object Detection
entry.summary: AxisQ: Depth-Adaptive Channel--Frequency Quantization for Camouflaged Object Detection arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper introduces AxisQ, a post-training quantization framework for camouflaged object detection models. It allocates bit precision in the channel domain for shallow features and in the local-frequency domain for deep features under a fixed bit budget, guided by COD-aware sensitivity and a boundary-aware Hessian approximation. Experiments report better accuracy than strong baselines at low bit widths, with relative weighted F-measure gains of 12.7% for CFRN and 33.3% for CamoFormer-P on CAMO under W2A2 quantization.

entry.title: MVRCap: Comprehensive Video Captioning with Hierarchical Multi-Dimensional Verifiable Rewards
entry.summary: MVRCap: Towards Comprehensive Video Captioning via Hierarchical Multi-Dimensional Verifiable Rewards arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper introduces MVRCap, a framework that treats video captioning as a reinforcement learning task guided by structured verification. Its core is a fine-grained verifiable reward with three parts: a hierarchical concept coverage reward, a factuality verification reward, and a conciseness constraint. The authors also build the MVRCap-QA and MVRCap-SFT datasets. The paper reports state-of-the-art results on benchmarks including VDC, CAPability, and VC4VG.

entry.title: Boosting-based joint distributional copula model for insurance claim frequency and severity
entry.summary: Joint Distributional Copula Regression for Insurance Claim Frequency and Severity via Boosting arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes a model-based boosting method for fitting structured additive distributional copula regression models with bivariate responses, focusing on jointly modeling claim frequency and claim severity. The approach builds on generalized additive models for location, scale, and shape (GAMLSS), allowing multiple distribution parameters to depend on covariates and keeping the model interpretable at the additive predictor level. Evaluations on synthetic and real-world data show that it recovers covariate effects and dependence structure, identifies informative variables, and achieves competitive predictive performance against benchmark models.]

entry.title: "Drop the Details, Get the Gist": A paper on dynamic concept representations for video recognition
entry.summary: Drop the Details, Get the Gist: Dynamic Conceptual Representation for Video Recognition arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper extends concept-based image recognition to video by representing a multi-step video as a temporal sequence of segment-level concept score vectors, which a Transformer encoder uses to predict the class label. It also explores estimating each concept's contribution to improve interpretability. Tests on cooking and household-activity videos with three concept sets of different granularity found that coarser-grained concepts are sufficient for classification.

entry.title: Right Click, Wrong Box: Judging GUI Clicks by Their Outcomes
entry.summary: Right Click, Wrong Box: Grading GUI Grounding by What a Click Does arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper argues that GUI grounding benchmarks count a click as correct only inside one annotated box, even though interfaces often expose the same action through several elements. The authors define a click as correct when it produces the same outcome as the annotated target, and build outcome maps and an execution judge by executing about a thousand clicks per page on live web applications.
