Testing three strong grounders on a code forge and an online shop, they find that many box-rejected clicks still reach the intended outcome, and an audit on ScreenSpot-v2 yields corrections of 0.2 to 1.8 points. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors grade GUI clicks by outcome rather than annotated box, reporting that roughly one in five to one in three box-rejected clicks reach the intended result, a shift comparable to reported mode

entry.title: When the Critic Falls Behind: Co-Evolving Rubrics and Harnesses for Continual Agent Self-Improvement
entry.summary: When the Critic Falls Behind: Co-Evolving Rubrics and Harnesses for Continual Agent Self-Improvement arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes RuHarness, a framework in which an AI agent's evaluation rubrics and its execution harness evolve together during continual self-improvement. It continually discovers and reassesses behavioral criteria from execution trajectories, prioritizes the most relevant unresolved weaknesses, and uses them to guide targeted harness updates while the task objective stays fixed. Experiments across diverse agent tasks and backbone models show it outperforms strong harness-evolution baselines, especially on unseen held-out tasks.

entry.title: Who knows what, and what does it support? Evidence calibration for multimodal theory of mind
entry.summary: Who Knows What - and What Does It Support? Perspective-Bounded Evidence Calibration for Multimodal Theory of Mind arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper addresses multimodal theory of mind, inferring an agent's beliefs, goals, and intentions from only the evidence available to that agent. The authors propose PIP-ToM, which builds agent-specific evidence stores, aligns them with structured mental-state claims, and calibrates hypothesis scores while keeping the Bayesian inference process. With GPT-4o, PIP-ToM reports average accuracies of 92.56% on MuMA-ToM, 95.00% on MMToM-QA, and 95.00% on Hi-ToM, outperforming existing ToM methods.

entry.title: TAPESTRY: One Backbone for Video Generation and Robot Control
entry.summary: TAPESTRY: A Single Backbone for Video Generation and Robot Control arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents TAPESTRY, which repurposes a pretrained video diffusion transformer into a robot policy by treating actions as single-patch tokens in the video latent space. The shared backbone is trained with three diffusion objectives, and at inference it produces a compact action token sequence in a single DDIM step without generating video. It runs at 84 ms per action chunk on consumer hardware. The authors report strong performance in simulation and real-robot experiments at substantially lower inference cost than comparable joint video-action policies.

entry.title: Incremental Knowledge-Graph Digital Twin for Evidence-Based Early Warning
entry.summary: An Incremental Knowledge-Graph Learner Digital Twin for Evidence-Grounded Early Warning arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents a lightweight, incremental learner digital twin built as a knowledge graph to support early warning in learning analytics. The twin is updated at temporal checkpoints by replaying learning traces and assessment records, and predictive features are extracted through graph queries. Evaluated on a public learning-analytics benchmark under a temporal protocol, graph-mediated features matched the predictive behavior of raw-table features, and generated alerts were linked to traceable evidence chains.

entry.title: Variable-length feedback coding with universal decoding and bandit channel selection
entry.summary: Variable-Length Feedback Coding With Universal Decoding and Bandit Channel Selection arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies variable-length feedback coding over K additive white Gaussian noise channels whose noise variances are unknown to both ends but lie in a known interval. The receiver picks one channel at each time, reports the choice over noiseless feedback, and learns channel quality while decoding. The authors propose two joint coding and channel-selection schemes, VLSF-Bandit and VLF-Bandit, and prove second-order achievability bounds for both.

entry.title: Words or Deeds? How LLMs Predict User Decisions in Human-Agent Dialogue
entry.summary: Words or Deeds? How LLMs Predict Users' Decisions in Human-Agent Dialogue arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This study examines how large language models combine users' statements with their past decision records to predict whether users will cooperate in a repeated prisoner's dilemma-style game. Forty-two users played 1,260 rounds against five agents, each expressing a different Big Five trait, and could talk with the agent before each decision. Decision records alone separated cooperation from defection well, and adding dialogue gave no detectable gain. Predictions leaned too heavily on users' statements, so errors were largest when users broke their promises.

entry.title: Weakness Localization Is Not Enough: State-Aware Recursive Knowledge Improvement for LLMs
entry.summary: Weakness Localization Is Not Enough: State-Aware Recursive Knowledge Improvement for Large Language Models arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper argues that localizing a large language model's knowledge weaknesses does not determine how to fix them, since the same weakness can stem from different knowledge states. The authors propose Recursive Knowledge Improvement (RKI), which organizes knowledge into graph-structured units and, each round, estimates the model's knowledge state to select an intervention before re-evaluating. On HotpotEval and SafeInternalEval, RKI outperforms existing knowledge incorporation methods by 18.41 points on average.

entry.title: Latent Visual Contrastive Reasoning with Multi-Branch Exploration: a method letting models explore several visual clues in parallel
entry.summary: Latent Visual Contrastive Reasoning with Multi-Branch Exploration arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper addresses complex visual reasoning in multimodal large language models, which often must locate and compare several question-relevant image regions. It proposes Latent Visual Contrastive Reasoning, which generates multiple question-conditioned latent visual branches as soft hypotheses over image tokens, trained with bounding-box evidence annotations and a soft contrastive branch-evidence alignment objective. Instantiated on Qwen2.5-VL at 3B and 7B scales, the method reports overall gains over the backbone and single-path latent reasoning baselines on perception-intensive visual reasoning benchmarks.

entry.title: SetGRPO: Calibrating Grader-Induced Policy Optimization
entry.summary: SetGRPO: Calibrating Grader-Induced Policy Optimization arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies how randomness in graders used for rubric-based reinforcement learning can alter GRPO training updates, beyond what score discrepancies alone reveal. It proposes Set-Valued Group Relative Policy Optimization (SetGRPO), built from three modules: joint reward set calibration, geometry-guided safe recovery, and selective risk-gated optimization to control direction-reversal risk. The authors report that on ten open-ended benchmarks across three domains, SetGRPO achieves the highest macro average among compared methods on Qwen3.5 and Llama3.2 model families.

entry.title: Using LLM-elicited priors to improve out-of-distribution tabular prediction via cross-validated regularisation
entry.summary: LLM knowledge for improved Out-of-Distribution Tabular Prediction - A Cross-Validated Regularisation Approach arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper addresses the problem that prediction models degrade when deployment populations differ from training populations. It uses coefficient priors elicited from large language models as the shrinkage target of a regularised regression instead of zero, testing out-of-distribution prediction on five tabular datasets, with providers and prior structures selected only by source-domain cross-validation. The priors improved results on four of five datasets, by up to 7.9% in out-of-distribution mean squared error, though variation across candidate priors exceeded the average benefit. On some datasets the gain in in-domain accuracy matched the out-of-domain gain, and elicited knowledge clearly improved transfer only where training data were large enough that the in-domain gain disappeared.

entry.title: Personality Latents: conditioning frozen language models on individuals' own writing
entry.summary: Personality Latents: Conditioning Frozen Language Models on Individuals from Their Own Writing arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper proposes Personality Latents (PL), which learn a latent representation for each person from their own writing, without personality labels or authored profiles, and inject it into a frozen language model as a soft prefix. An encoder predicts these latents so a new person needs one forward pass, with optional test-time refinement. On held-out people, PL outperforms persona embedding and prompt-based baselines on MBTI axes, and the ranking holds across three embedding spaces. A latent learned with Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct also transfers personality to Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct through a new adapter alone.

entry.title: API-TAIL: Detecting Hidden Model Swaps in LLM APIs Using Temperature-Aligned Likelihood Tails
entry.summary: API-TAIL: Detecting Model Substitution in LLM APIs through Temperature-Aligned Likelihood Tails arXiv · Oct 27, 2026Commercial language model APIs return only text, so a provider could secretly route some requests to a cheaper model while billing for the advertised one. The paper introduces API-TAIL, an audit that first aligns an effective temperature to remove batch-wide shifts caused by legitimate settings, then counts remaining anomalous responses against a calibrated threshold. Tested on real commercial APIs, it controls false alarms and detects low-rate partial substitution with few queries, outperforming existing rank- and MMD-based audits.

entry.title: Language Models Keep Abandoned Analyses: Residue and Adaptation after Garden-Path Sentences
entry.summary: Language Models Keep Abandoned Analyses: Residue and Adaptation after Garden-Path Sentences arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper examines whether language models keep using syntactic analyses they have abandoned after reading garden-path sentences. Across 24 open models, the authors find a residue of the abandoned analysis that raises later object attachment, plus an adaptation toward the resolved structure. Activation patching shows the residue is carried by noun-phrase states computed before disambiguation, and replacing them removes most of it in the larger models. ★★★★ Notable: Activation patching separates residue from adaptation after garden-path sentences across 24 open models, also testing persistence of overridden statements and transfer to the human paradigm.

entry.title: An algebra for reasoning about Transformers
entry.summary: An Algebra of Transformers arXiv · Oct 27, 2026Prior theoretical work on Transformers mainly studies computability, such as Turing-completeness and parallelizability for unbounded precision and limitations for bounded precision. This paper builds an algebra for reasoning about Transformers, relying on functional decomposition results of Transformers. It treats functional decompositions as atomic actions and includes sequential and parallel composition, recursion for feedback, and abstraction for hidden layers. The authors describe it as the first attempt to model Transformers logically, usable for verifying the correctness of Transformer-based applications.

entry.title: Select-TTT: Query-Guided Selective Weight Updates for Test-Time Training
entry.summary: Select-TTT: Query-Conditioned Selective Fast Weight Updates for In-Place Test-Time Training arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies test-time training, where a deployed language model stores incoming long context in a small set of fast weights. It finds that In-Place TTT, which writes every context chunk with equal strength, loses its benefit on realistic web long-context question answering because irrelevant content dilutes useful information. The proposed Select-TTT scales each chunk's write strength by its relevance to the user query, measured from the frozen output head without supervision or new parameters. The method consistently improves long-context question answering on two benchmarks and two backbone models.

entry.title: Visual Autoregressive Generation with Next Token Imagination: Letting Models Explore Plausible Images Beyond Training Data
entry.summary: Visual Autoregressive Generation with Next Token Imagination arXiv · Oct 27, 2026Visual autoregressive models are normally trained only on the ground-truth next token, which limits how much of the visual distribution they learn. This paper proposes Next Token Imagination (NTI), which lets the model explore alternatives beyond the ground-truth next token under a criterion that keeps this exploration bounded by the visual distribution. Experiments on ImageNet show NTI consistently and substantially improves generated image fidelity, approaching state-of-the-art diffusion and autoregressive models with a smaller model and lower training cost.

entry.title: OmniGlimpse: An Asymmetric Identity Memory Method for Online Multi-View Tracking
entry.summary: OmniGlimpse: Asymmetric Identity Memory for Online Multi-View Tracking arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies online multi-view identity maintenance, which matches observations from different cameras to the correct targets without offline scene-specific training or camera calibration. The authors propose OmniGlimpse, an asymmetric propose-verify framework that separates adaptive short-term association from stable long-term identity consolidation. On the M3Track and MvMHAT benchmarks, it improves over the best evaluated online baseline on IDF1 and CVIDF1, and outperforms offline-trained references on IDF1.

entry.title: CVBL-CCTV-Face Dataset: Real-World Face Enhancement and Recognition for Surveillance
entry.summary: CVBL-CCTV-Face Dataset for Real-World Face Enhancement and Recognition in Surveillance arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper addresses how low resolution, motion blur, noise, and occlusion in CCTV face captures undermine reliable face recognition. The authors propose a framework for super-resolution and identity recognition for surveillance, and present the CVBL-CCTV-Face Dataset, which pairs low-quality face images from an 8MP IP dome CCTV camera with high-quality reference images taken in controlled settings in an unpaired manner. The modular system combines face detection, deep learning-based super-resolution, and identity recognition using L2-normalized embeddings. Enhancement models are trained and tested under three setups, and the system is deployed for identity verification in a real-time unconstrained environment.

entry.title: Does LLM pre-training usually happen at the edge of stability?
entry.summary: Does LLM Pre-Training Typically Occur at the Edge of Stability? arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper revisits how well quadratic approximations model neural network training, especially in large language model (LLM) pretraining. It identifies an "Edge of Convexity" (EoC) failure mode, where persistent negative curvature makes the quadratic dynamics diverge regardless of learning rate, and proposes a generalized Edge of Stability (EoS) definition for stochastic adaptive optimizers. Across LLM pretraining runs with models up to 787M parameters, EoC is always observed, while EoS is common but not universal, disappearing at sufficiently small learning rates or batch sizes below a critical threshold. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes a learning-rate-independent Edge of Convexity and generalizes Edge of Stability to stochastic training with adaptive optimizers; the authors report EoC consistently appears and EoS is common

entry.title: Graphs tracking how mathematical arguments depend on earlier steps, for review and measurement
entry.summary: Dependency Graphs of Mathematical Arguments: Representation, Structural Measurement, and Proof Review arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper proposes a framework that uses large language models to represent mathematical arguments as dependency graphs linking statements, equations, and assumptions to their sources. It defines structural measures such as depth, the longest prerequisite path, and bulk, the count of distinct ancestor edges, along with a standardized prompt protocol. The authors provide an evaluation design rather than empirical results, and note that suggested premises need mathematical validation and the measures describe the representation, not intrinsic difficulty or importance.

entry.title: Running Several Candidate Edits at Once to Speed Up AI Prompt Tuning
entry.summary: Batching the Reflective Optimization Loop: Parallel Proposals Make GEPA Faster and Better arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper extends the open-source GEPA optimizer so that each optimization step proposes and evaluates a batch of candidates rather than one at a time. In experiments on two tasks, most batched runs finished in half the wall-clock time or less, and the fastest in about a quarter to a third. Batched settings also scored higher on held-out tests. The authors offer a simple runtime model for the speedups under a finite worker pool and an initial look at splitting a fixed budget across parallel axes.

entry.title: Can LLMs Reliably Grade Olympiad Proofs? A Study of Math Proof Verification
entry.summary: Can LLMs Reliably Grade Olympiad Proofs? A Study of Mathematical Verification with LLMs arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper systematically studies whether large language models can verify natural-language mathematical proofs at the Olympiad level. The authors build an expert-graded dataset of USAMO 2025 candidate solutions and introduce TROJAN, an iterative self-critique pipeline for generating adversarial proofs at scale. They also propose MABGrader, a multi-armed bandit framework that outperforms the state-of-the-art ProofGrader by 26.4% in Quadratic Weighted Kappa and reduces grading error by 14%.

entry.title: Evaluation-Guided Demonstration Refinement for Vision-Language-Action Policies: Winning MetaFine Competition Entry
entry.summary: Evaluation-Guided Demonstration Refinement for Vision-Language-Action Policies: The Winning Entry in the MetaFine Open Competition arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents the winning entry in the MetaFine Open Competition. The authors fine-tuned a separate π0.5 policy for each of five tasks, revising demonstrated motions and adding expert continuations from states the policy reached to address grasping, pushing, and insertion failures. Checkpoints were compared on every instruction, and the submission, MAI, ranked first overall with a score of 96.66.

entry.title: Beyond the Evidence Coherence Trap: Agent-Driven Evidence Selection for Detecting Temporally Disordered Fake News
entry.summary: Beyond the Evidence Coherence Trap: Agent-Driven Evidence Selection for Temporally Disordered Fake News Detection arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper addresses fake news that rearranges real events into a false chronology, where individual facts may be accurate but their timing is misrepresented. The authors describe an "evidence coherence trap" in which retrieved evidence from a similar event in the wrong period leads to incorrect verification. They introduce ChronoFake, a benchmark of 30,706 articles, and propose DelSA, an agent that iteratively refines evidence selection and compares article and evidence chronologies to expose temporal conflicts. DelSA outperforms existing methods on ChronoFake and remains competitive on PolitiFact and GossipCop.

entry.title: The Vocabulary Is Already Here: Adapting Pretrained Interpretable Features for Generative Recommendation
entry.summary: The Vocabulary Is Already Here: Adapting Pretrained Interpretable Features for Generative Recommendation arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes API, a framework that reuses feature indices from pretrained sparse autoencoders as a semantic ID vocabulary for generative recommendation, without learning a new vocabulary. It introduces Pretrained Interpretable IDs and a Semantic Prediction Adapter that jointly predicts feature indices and activation strengths from interaction histories. Experiments report competitive performance across backbones and decoding schemes, along with explainable retrieval through feature contributions.

entry.title: Making Self-Driving Labs Auditable: A Unified Framework for Safe, Traceable Automated Experiments
entry.summary: Making Self-Driving Laboratories Auditable:A Unified Framework for Hybrid Actions,Measurements, and Safe Execution arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper addresses the challenge of connecting flexible robot control with laboratory instrument interfaces in self-driving laboratories (SDLs). It proposes four components: LAM (Lab Action Model) for generating robot trajectories and instrument API calls, OpenSDL as an execution substrate, Safe-SDL as a runtime safety gate, and L3-Bench as an evaluation protocol. Together they provide an end-to-end design linking action generation, monitored execution, measurement feedback, and experimental evaluation.

entry.title: GeoGSplat: Geometry-Grounded Non-Pixel-Aligned Gaussian Splatting for View Synthesis
entry.summary: GeoGSplat: Geometry-Grounded Non-Pixel-Aligned Gaussian Splatting arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents GeoGSplat, a feed-forward Gaussian Splatting model that adds geometric priors to a non-pixel-aligned framework to fix misplaced Gaussian centers. A dual-branch encoder captures coarse 3D structure and fine scene features, and a hierarchical decoder progressively generates dense 3D points and Gaussian primitives. The model outperforms prior pixel-aligned and non-pixel-aligned methods on DTU and NRGBD for novel view synthesis and reconstruction, with the advantage growing as target views move farther from the input cameras.

entry.title: DocSkill: Agentic reasoning for multilingual multi-hop document question answering
entry.summary: DocSkill: Skill-Integrated Agentic Reasoning for Multilingual Multi-Hop Document Question Answering arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents DocSkill, an agentic framework that uses a learned policy to select, revisit, or skip skills while gathering evidence and reasoning over multilingual documents. Skill trajectories are generated offline with bounded Monte Carlo Tree Search and used for supervised fine-tuning and Direct Preference Optimization. The authors also introduce MMHop-DocBench, a dataset of 60K QA pairs across 10 languages and eight document domains. With Qwen3-VL-8B, DocSkill reaches 41.0 accuracy and 49.2 F1 on MMHop-DocBench, outperforming the strongest baseline, and performs competitively on MMLongBench-Doc and DocBench.

entry.title: Reinforcement learning for diffusions with step-size-independent logarithmic regret
entry.summary: Frequency-Uniform Log-Regret Reinforcement Learning for Diffusions arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper studies episodic value-based reinforcement learning for Euler discretizations of controlled diffusions, measuring performance by cumulative regret against the optimal policy of the Euler model. Under stability and regularity conditions, it proves an O(log K) regret bound whose constants do not depend on the timestep δ. For drift linear in unknown parameters with unknown constant diffusion covariance, it introduces a constrained model-based fitted-Q algorithm (CD-FQ) and obtains a high-probability O(log K log log K) regret bound.

entry.title: Faster remote sensing image-text retrieval using interaction-free recall and text-guided reranking.
entry.summary: Efficient Remote Sensing Image-Text Retrieval via Interaction-Free Recall and Text-Guided Reranking arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes a fast-then-fine (FTF) framework for cross-modal retrieval between remote sensing images and text. It combines interaction-free multi-granular recall with parameter-free text-guided reranking of top-K candidates using a Balanced Text-guided Interaction Block (BTIB). An inter- and intra-modal loss is also designed to jointly optimize alignment across multi-granular representations. The authors report competitive accuracy and significantly improved efficiency on public benchmarks.

entry.title: Robust LLM Data Selection via Content-Invariant Gradient Attribution
entry.summary: Robust LLM Data Selection via Content-Invariant Gradient Attribution arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper shows that existing gradient-based data attribution methods for LLM instruction tuning are sensitive to surface-form changes such as wording or formatting, which can shift scores even when content is unchanged. It proposes CIGA, which selects layers whose gradients are both influential and stable under semantics-preserving perturbations, then fuses these signals with input semantic representations. Experiments across benchmarks report more stable rankings, improved average performance, and lower attribution cost.

entry.title: Learning to correct interpolation for reconstructing intermediate scientific fields
entry.summary: Generative Refinement Learning for Temporal Interpolation in Scientific Machine Learning arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper proposes iFLEX, a method for reconstructing unobserved intermediate scientific fields between two observation times. It first forms a time-weighted average of the two observations, then uses a conditional diffusion model to learn and generate the residual between this average and the true intermediate field. The authors evaluate it on Navier-Stokes Kraichnan turbulence, Shanghai radar precipitation, and sea surface temperature data, reporting lower reconstruction error than the compared baselines. ★★★★ Notable: Over weighted averaging, a conditional diffusion model learns the residual; the authors report lower reconstruction error than optical-flow and video diffusion baselines on three scientific datasets.

entry.title: A multi-task Mamba-CNN model for MODIS spectral-temporal unmixing that accounts for endmember variability
entry.summary: Multi-task Disentangling Fusion Mamba-CNN for MODIS Spectral-Temporal Unmixing with Endmember Variability Modeling arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes MDF-Mamba, a model for estimating land-cover abundances from MODIS time series via spectral-temporal unmixing. It separates spectral and temporal information using per-channel spectral experts and a bidirectional Mamba temporal branch, then merges their outputs with a mHCFusion module. Pixel-wise learnable weights model intra-class endmember variability. On MODIS data from Alberta and Saskatchewan, the model achieves the best result on 12 of 14 evaluation metrics.

entry.title: Using neurons' biological identity to analyze how neural populations behave across animals
entry.summary: Neuronal Identity as an Organizational Basis for Analyzing Neural Population Dynamics arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes a framework that groups neurons into latent clusters based on their molecular, morphological, and electrophysiological profiles, then analyzes population dynamics through these group-level representations. Because the assignments rest on biological features shared across individuals, the learned organization transfers to unseen animals without retraining or neuron-to-neuron correspondence. The method is evaluated on whole-brain calcium imaging in larval zebrafish and large-scale electrophysiology in mouse visual cortex, where it reports stronger neural decoding and manifold analysis performance.

entry.title: Sensitivity of Readout and Operating Points in Event-Stream Candidate Selection
entry.summary: Readout and Operating-Point Sensitivity in Event-Stream Candidate Selection arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper examines the trade-off between capturing target events and triggering false alarms in event-triggered recording. Using real event accumulations from 520 DailyDVS-200 clips across 47 participants, it compares encoders, accumulation durations, and temporal view counts for candidate selection. The authors find that readout choices and threshold calibration can change which method appears better. They conclude the evidence covers only offline, action-defined selection and does not establish a JEPA-specific advantage.

entry.title: CAMR: A Method for Continual Learning in Large Language Models That Decides Which Examples to Learn and Replay
entry.summary: CAMR: Compatibility-Aware Memory Replay for Continual Learning in Large Language Models arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes CAMR, a continual learning framework for large language models that balances learning new information with retaining old knowledge. It uses compatibility checks and a learned memory gate to choose, for each incoming example, among learning with general replay, reinforcing compatible related examples, or skipping verified duplicates. Evaluated with Qwen3-8B-Base on factual updating and cross-task benchmarks, CAMR reports leading results over compared methods.

entry.title: Hy-Nomas: Free-form Interactive World Generation
entry.summary: Hy-Nomas: Towards Free-form Interactive World Generation arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents Hy-Nomas, an 8B diffusion-based video world model that follows free-form text instructions and continuous camera control across multiple interaction turns. It pairs structured video captions with action-aware causal attention, and uses a vision-language Prompt Enhancer to turn user requests and interaction histories into conditions for each segment. The model is trained with a multi-stage curriculum followed by diffusion distillation. The authors report superior human-evaluation results over existing world models and release weights, code and benchmarks.

entry.title: A method that progressively refines SAM to segment phytoplankton more accurately.
entry.summary: Progressively Refining SAM for Accurate Phytoplankton Segmentation arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes PhySeg, a segmentation framework built on SAM with a lightweight refinement module that gradually recovers fine details through multi-scale feature fusion. The authors also manually annotated instance-level masks on an existing dataset to create a phytoplankton segmentation dataset. Experiments show that PhySeg improves segmentation accuracy.

entry.title: SAGE: A Saliency-Annealed Gated Encoder for General Vision Recognition
entry.summary: SAGE: Saliency-Annealed Gated Encoder for Universal Vision Recognition arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes SAGE, an enhanced ViT-Adapter backbone that adapts self-supervised Vision Transformers to dense prediction by exploiting saliency, global context, and high-frequency details. It combines a saliency-guided architecture, an annealing-based training scheme, and a two-stage training mechanism that shifts from focal loss to Varifocal Loss. The authors report state-of-the-art or competitive results on COCO, COCO keypoints, ADE20K, TinyImageNet, and DIOR-R object detection, using one shared backbone with task-specific decoders.

entry.title: Nonlinear Direct Feedback Alignment: a scalable training method without backpropagation
entry.summary: Nonlinear Direct Feedback Alignment for Scalable Backpropagation-Free Training arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper addresses the biological implausibility and backward locking of backpropagation by improving Direct Feedback Alignment (DFA). The proposed Nonlinear Direct Feedback Alignment (NDFA) builds each hidden-layer feedback path with a lightweight nonlinear surrogate subnetwork, which is updated by a dedicated learning strategy. Experiments on residual networks and vision transformers across CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN, and ImageNet show that NDFA outperforms existing DFA-based methods and narrows the gap to backpropagation. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes NDFA, which replaces fixed DFA feedback with a lightweight nonlinear surrogate subnetwork updated during training; the authors report it beats prior DFA methods and narrows the gap to BP on C

entry.title: A harness that isolates objections to reduce agents' over-defensive writing
entry.summary: A Harness Reducing over-Defensive Writing in Agents by Isolating Objections arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper observes that agents expanding reports often write a stronger claim than the source supports and then disclaim it, which it calls over-defensive writing. The authors propose a harness that separates a reviewer, a filter, and a writer, so the writer sees only the problems chosen by the filter. In an evaluation on 25 business-project drafts expanded into formal reports, defensive propositions fell from 59 to 2, a 96.61% reduction, while source-claim retention rose from 80.35% to 93.12%.

entry.title: SMEBENCH: A Benchmark for Neural Music Editing with Synthesized MIDI Edits
entry.summary: SMEBENCH: Benchmarking Neural Music Editing with Synthetized MIDI Edits arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper introduces SMEBENCH, a large-scale benchmark for neural music editing. It is built by modifying symbolic MIDI performances and rendering matched source and target audio, covering twelve operations across instrumentation, articulation, dynamics, and pitch. The benchmark includes a balanced 3,600-example test set and a smaller real-audio complement from multitrack recordings. The authors use the paired targets to evaluate six representative editing systems and show that the metric used for ranking can significantly change the conclusions.
